I had been working with the great people on the Indivisible Auburn/Opelika Steering Committee. We held a "No Show Town Hall Meeting" for Mike Rogers in April, and the crowd outstripped anything we imagined. I MC'd the event and spoke about Congressman Rogers' failure to fulfill his responsibilities as the Chairman of the House Armed Services Committee.
Before I gave that speech, I was terrified. I had spent 30 years covered by the Hatch Act and wasn't allowed to participate in partisan politics. It was the first openly political speech I had ever given. The people at the event could not have been more supportive. A few even came up to me and said I should run for office. I laughed it all off.
The surprising part came next: as the protests continued, people would come up to me, shake my hand, tell me I did a great job, and ask me to run for Congress against Mike Rogers. Not run just for the sake of running for office, but specifically against Mike Rogers. Barb saw all of this, and we realized people's feelings about Mike Rogers ran pretty deep...

# One Last Thought Until Next Week
---
| | |
---
Over the last few weeks, we've been out meeting our neighbors at community celebrations.
It was great to see the surprise on people's faces when they realized I wasn't there supporting the candidate, but I am the candidate. I just told them that, when elected, I will be representing every community in the district, and the best way I know to show that is to show up at their community events and spend time talking to them. For members of our marginalized communities, that really had an impact.
We had another event this weekend. It was a small gathering in Wedowee, hosted by a friend. We sat, ate burgers, and talked with people from Randolph County we had not met before. Yes, these are campaign events, and I hope everyone who met me there will vote for me, but I was also there to hear what they had to say about their community. Some of the people there are activists supporting the immigrant community in Randolph County, and the stories they told about ICE operations in the county were heartbreaking. Others were seriously concerned about cuts to Medicare and Medicaid and the impact those cuts would have on their local hospital. I'm thankful we had time to talk so I could hear what they're worried about.
If all you do is show up at an event, climb out of your air-conditioned car, take a few pictures, and then leave, you're not meeting your constituents; you're using them as a backdrop for a photo op. Getting to know our neighbors is something we have been doing for a year. I hope we get the chance to keep it up into the future.
We are 140 days away from the general election.

We'll talk soon,

Lee

clean_body: You Don't Want to Miss This | | | | | == | | | CAMPAIGN UPDATE | | | MAKING HISTORY | | THE WEEK AHEAD | | Alabama Primary Election Runoff 🗓️ June 16 🕓 7 A.M. - 7 P.M. 📍 == | | A Seat at the Table: A Juneteenth Breakfast to Carry Memory Forward Hosted by the Lee County Remembrance Project 🗓️ June 19 🕓 9 A.M. 📍 The Nonprofit Center of East Alabama 1944 Opelika Road Suite 101 Auburn, AL | | | Lafayette Juneteenth Parade 🗓️ June 19 🕓 3 P.M. 📍 Begins in downtown LaFayette and leads into the back parking lot of Krave Korner | | Opelika Juneteenth Celebration 🗓️ June 19 🕓 5 P.M. - 8 P.M. 📍 Courthouse Square | | | THE WEEK BEHIND | | | | | | 🗓️ June 13: Auburn Juneteenth Celebration These events are the highlight of the campaign. We spent five hours at the park, talked with some great people, and being there for that long gives you the chance to really talk to people, hear their concerns, and find out what they need from their elected representatives. | | | In Case You Missed It | BLOG POSTS | == Back in the fall of 2025, we were in Roanoke. A woman was walking by, and I introduced myself. She paused, nodded her head, and said, "I've never voted for a Democrat before, but I probably will this time." I never let that go. I always want to know why. She explained that she had a child with significant learning disabilities, and as of the first of the year, most of the programs her child depended on were going to be cut. The school board had "reprioritized the budget," and those programs hadn't made the cut. I asked if she had talked to anyone, and she said she had. She called the school board, and they wouldn't talk to her, not even to explain what was more important than her child's education. She called the state board of education, and they told her she should call the US Department of Education, which she did. I knew what that answer would be. There were two offices in the Education Department that should have been able to help her, and they had both been gutted... | == I had been working with the great people on the Indivisible Auburn/Opelika Steering Committee. We held a "No Show Town Hall Meeting" for Mike Rogers in April, and the crowd outstripped anything we imagined. I MC'd the event and spoke about Congressman Rogers' failure to fulfill his responsibilities as the Chairman of the House Armed Services Committee. Before I gave that speech, I was terrified. I had spent 30 years covered by the Hatch Act and wasn't allowed to participate in partisan politics. It was the first openly political speech I had ever given. The people at the event could not have been more supportive. A few even came up to me and said I should run for office. I laughed it all off. The surprising part came next: as the protests continued, people would come up to me, shake my hand, tell me I did a great job, and ask me to run for Congress against Mike Rogers. Not run just for the sake of running for office, but specifically against Mike Rogers. Barb saw all of this, and we realized people's feelings about Mike Rogers ran pretty deep... | == | A Few Things to Think About | | | ALABAMA IN THE NEWS | 📰 == The Alabama Department of Veterans Affairs has appointed Andrea Searor as its first Women Veterans Coordinator, a new position created to expand outreach and support for women veterans across the state. Searor, a retired Air Force leader with 26 years of service, will work to connect women veterans with healthcare, benefits, and other resources at a time when more than 43,000 women veterans live in Alabama. State officials said the role reflects a commitment to addressing the unique needs of women veterans and improving access to services and support. | 📰 == Google announced a $1.5 billion investment to expand its data center campus in Jackson County, bringing additional jobs, construction activity, and economic development to northeast Alabama. Alongside the expansion, the company pledged funding for energy affordability programs, STEM education initiatives, and local infrastructure projects, including a $2 million fund to help reduce energy costs for area residents. The announcement reflects Alabama's growing role as a hub for data center development, as major technology companies continue investing in the state's available land, energy resources, and strategic location to support increasing demand for cloud computing and artificial intelligence infrastructure. | 📰 == Local economic development officials are organizing a job fair in Talladega County after the sudden closure of Legacy Cabinets in Eastaboga left approximately 370 workers without jobs. Former employees say they received little warning about the shutdown and have raised questions about final paychecks, benefits, and whether the company complied with federal WARN Act notification requirements. The closure marks the second major plant shutdown in east Alabama this year, highlighting ongoing concerns about economic stability and workforce support in the region. | A CALL TO ACTION | Volunteer: We're building a strong volunteer team to power the campaign through the general election, and we need your help. Sign up below to help move this campaign forward. | == | Follow Us: We need you to like, comment on, and share our social media posts. We also need you to talk to your friends about the campaign. We need you to come to any events we have in your area so your friends can see they're not alone. | == == == | | | Donate: Your contribution helps us keep our campaign moving by funding outreach, events, and voter engagement efforts across the district. | | == | | One Last Thought Until Next Week | | | Over the last few weeks, we've been out meeting our neighbors at community celebrations. It was great to see the surprise on people's faces when they realized I wasn't there supporting the candidate, but I am the candidate. I just told them that, when elected, I will be representing every community in the district, and the best way I know to show that is to show up at their community events and spend time talking to them. For members of our marginalized communities, that really had an impact. We had another event this weekend. It was a small gathering in Wedowee, hosted by a friend. We sat, ate burgers, and talked with people from Randolph County we had not met before. Yes, these are campaign events, and I hope everyone who met me there will vote for me, but I was also there to hear what they had to say about their community. Some of the people there are activists supporting the immigrant community in Randolph County, and the stories they told about ICE operations in the county were heartbreaking. Others were seriously concerned about cuts to Medicare and Medicaid and the impact those cuts would have on their local hospital. I'm thankful we had time to talk so I could hear what they're worried about. If all you do is show up at an event, climb out of your air-conditioned car, take a few pictures, and then leave, you're not meeting your constituents; you're using them as a backdrop for a photo op. Getting to know our neighbors is something we have been doing for a year. I hope we get the chance to keep it up into the future. We are 140 days away from the general election. name: Roy Cooper
subject: They can’t scare me into backing down
body:
I am ready for the fight.
Peter,
Stop the chaos.
Peter, this is what elected leaders must do in the face of an administration that is intent on destroying our democracy for their own gain.
I have spent my career working for North Carolinians. Advocating for more resources for students in public schools and better pay for teachers. Building a clean energy economy to bring good-paying jobs to our communities while protecting this planet. Defending the right to cast a ballot and participate in our democracy. Fighting for Medicaid Expansion and winning it for the people. **I stand ready to do all this and more to deliver for the American people as the next Democratic Senator from North Carolina.**
_Far-right Republicans don’t tend to like that about me — and they don’t want me bringing this fight to Washington._
They’re preparing to spend untold sums trying to take me down.
But I know how to win here. **And I will not back down.**
_Because I have you on my side._
**[Peter, this is the most consequential Senate race of the midterms. It’s the seat that can take back the majority, break the GOP’s hold on Washington and return power to the people. It won’t be easy, but we can succeed together. I’m humbly asking you to pitch in today and split a donation between our campaign and Wes Moore (any amount will help) to stand with me in the fight.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260616-2.rSlsql&refcode=em-20260616-2&t=1&akid=1501%2E1086043%2EM0tvT4)**

I couldn’t do this without you. Thank you.
Roy

| | Friend,

I have some big news to share: **I am officially the Democratic nominee for Wisconsin Secretary of State.**

Now the real work begins.That means our entire focus, starting right now, is on November and on building the kind of campaign that wins statewide and lifts up every Democrat on the ballot.
---
| [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/D_3JAKzmeNt?e=8d919f2092&c2id=0bdcb6d83cbc8b2aaf05afb952b88bb7)
---
| This past weekend, I had the honor of addressing the Wisconsin Democratic convention. Standing in front of a room full of organizers, volunteers, and neighbors from every corner of this state, I felt the energy behind this campaign in a way I won't soon forget. This is what we are building together.

**I do not take this moment for granted**. I grew up on the south side of Milwaukee, the daughter of a single mom who worked multiple jobs to keep us going. I learned early what it means to stretch every dollar, and I carry those families with me in everything I do. They are the reason I am in this race.

The stakes could not be higher. This office may not come with sweeping powers, but it comes with a platform, and I will use it to fight for working families, defend the freedom to vote, and stand up for a Wisconsin that works for everyone.

**I am ready for that fight. But I cannot do it without you.**

[We have set a critical fundraising goal to hit by midnight on June 30th. ](https://us.list-manage.com/ZAdN7syW_58?e=8d919f2092&c2id=0bdcb6d83cbc8b2aaf05afb952b88bb7)This is how we launch this general election campaign with the momentum to organize in every corner of the state, from Kenosha to Superior.

| | | | JoCasta Zamarripa is a lifelong Milwaukeean, a proud daughter of the city’s south side, and a dedicated public servant who’s never stopped fighting for working people. Born and raised in the very neighborhoods she now represents, JoCasta has spent her life pushing for progress that reflects the realities of everyday Wisconsinites.

[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/OD7C1NusqdO?e=8d919f2092&c2id=0bdcb6d83cbc8b2aaf05afb952b88bb7)

She made history as the first Latina and first openly bi member of both the Wisconsin State Legislature and the Milwaukee Common Council. But JoCasta’s leadership is defined by more than her historic firsts—it's grounded in results. She served ten years in the State Assembly and is now in her second term as Alderperson for Milwaukee’s 8th District, where she’s led major efforts on affordable housing, small business licensing reform, and community development.

In 2025, she was the lead sponsor of the Housing Element Plan, a key step in addressing Milwaukee’s housing crisis by expanding affordable options and preventing displacement. Her approach is practical and persistent—building coalitions, navigating political challenges, and staying rooted in the neighborhoods she serves.

Now, JoCasta is running as a Democrat for Wisconsin Secretary of State to use the platform to fight for what matters: more funding for our schools so families aren’t forced into referenda every election, real housing relief for working people, and affordable child care that lets parents breathe.

clean_body: We cannot let them see weakness. Not now. | Fellow American - I need your help. I just won my primary. But I won't pretend that the fight was free. Our campaign coffers took a hit, and we're heading into the mid-month running lean. That's a problem because we're also just weeks away from the end-of-quarter deadline, and you can bet Democrats are watching our FEC report like a hawk. Let me remind you what we're up against. In 2020, my Democrat opponent raised $132 MILLION trying to defeat me. Last year alone, my current Democrat challenger hauled in $1.2 million in just 30 days. And now that we're in the thick of Election Year 2026, the national Democrats are flooding South Carolina with even more cash. The Hollywood liberals. The radical Super PACs. The Democratic insiders in Washington - they see South Carolina as a target. They always have. I've been in tough fights before. I don't scare easily. But I also don't take anything for granted. This campaign runs because of grassroots conservatives like you. Not Washington insiders. Not Hollywood elites. Not the radical Left. You are the backbone of Team Graham. With the end-of-quarter deadline just weeks away, our fundraising numbers will be public. This number will tell our opponents everything they need to know about whether South Carolina is vulnerable. We cannot let them see weakness. Not now. If we're going to keep South Carolina strong, defend conservative values, and stop the Left's agenda in its tracks, we have to hit our June numbers. South Carolina is worth fighting for. With your help, we'll win again. * **Closing outlook stated** : Transactions expected third quarter close with details on July earnings call and $85 million one time expenses.

_**By David Shuster**_
If the Trump White House had a mascot, it would be the screwworm. The parasite is a vulgar creature that makes everything it touches worse.
The screwworm lays its eggs in the wounds of living animals, and the resulting larvae proceeds to consume flesh with the diligence and appetite of Donald Trump's approach to Big Macs.
For 60 years, the loathsome and expensive screwworm was largely controlled. Then the Trump 2nd term geniuses arrived.
Trump administration 2.0, with the help of Elon Musk, promised a revolution in government efficiency.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dcde13a9-fb2e-4fe3-ac71-ec0388c309db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) we were told, would eliminate waste. In turn, Musk's DOGE fired hundreds of thousands of government workers.
Some of those workers had the responsibility of monitoring and containing screwworm outbreaks in Central America. The reason for their work was obvious to anyone capable of connecting cause and effect. The cheapest place to stop a parasite is before it reaches your border. The cheapest outbreak is the one that never occurs.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dcde13a9-fb2e-4fe3-ac71-ec0388c309db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But under the Trump administration's DOGE initiative, screwworm monitoring was cut. Not after the threat had vanished. Not because experts declared the mission accomplished. It was cut while the threat remained active and, astonishingly, just days before the Trump administration lifted restrictions on cattle imports from Mexico.
Agricultural officials warned against it. Ranchers warned against it. Livestock experts warned against it.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.Rh0bUSOuyksDoEBonivPro9oS2mCrPOr9V2OZgEAw5g?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=202187350)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dcde13a9-fb2e-4fe3-ac71-ec0388c309db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Texas Agriculture Commissioner Sid Miller says that he and other state officials spent months sounding alarms as screwworm infections moved steadily northward through Mexico.
They might as well have been shouting at an unconscious or napping Trump.
And even when Trump is awake, our government has little use for expertise. People who actually understand a problem are viewed as obstacles to the glorious simplicity of cutting budgets.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=202187350&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjAyMTg3MzUwLCJpYXQiOjE3ODE2MzQwNzEsImV4cCI6MTc4NDIyNjA3MSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.OYtFnLt9XjE9YB1Oxa09PHxRbPrL12AnPwYpBKXGA_8)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dcde13a9-fb2e-4fe3-ac71-ec0388c309db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Why listen to veterinarians when there are Elon Musk spreadsheets? Why heed inspectors when there are press releases? Why concern oneself with biology when Trump has already fallen in love with ideology?
The screwworm, unfortunately, proved stubbornly indifferent to branding strategies.
Now the consequences are arriving precisely as predicted. Cases in the U.S. are soaring. Cattle restrictions are tightening. Ranchers are facing greater risks. Beef supplies are diminishing. And consumers are paying more. Prices have risen 16% in just the past year. A two pound ribeye steak now costs $22.
[Leave a comment](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=202187350&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&isFreemail=true&comments=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjAyMTg3MzUwLCJpYXQiOjE3ODE2MzQwNzEsImV4cCI6MTc4NDIyNjA3MSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.OYtFnLt9XjE9YB1Oxa09PHxRbPrL12AnPwYpBKXGA_8&r=1hvr60&utm_campaign=email-half-magic-comments&action=post-comment)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dcde13a9-fb2e-4fe3-ac71-ec0388c309db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And what magnificent savings did Trump and Musk achieve? The public has never been told. Because the Trump apostles of austerity never linger to calculate the costs that emerge after their celebrated cuts. They count the dollars saved today and ignore the extra millions spent tomorrow.
This is not efficiency. It is vandalism masquerading as management.
Real efficiency requires understanding what a system actually does. It requires distinguishing between bureaucracy that exists merely to perpetuate itself and institutions that perform essential work.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.Rh0bUSOuyksDoEBonivPro9oS2mCrPOr9V2OZgEAw5g?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=202187350)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dcde13a9-fb2e-4fe3-ac71-ec0388c309db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
A program preventing a flesh-eating parasite from reaching the North American cattle industry is not ornamental. It is not a luxury. It is not some decadent indulgence dreamed up by idle civil servants. It is one of the basic maintenance functions of a modern agricultural filled economy.
Yet modern politics, under Trump, has often rewarded theatrical gestures rather than competent administration. The politician who quietly funds disease surveillance receives no applause. The politician (usually a republican) who abolishes it receives headlines, interviews, and social media celebrations for "cutting waste." Months later, when the predictable consequences emerge, everyone acts mystified.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=202187350&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjAyMTg3MzUwLCJpYXQiOjE3ODE2MzQwNzEsImV4cCI6MTc4NDIyNjA3MSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.OYtFnLt9XjE9YB1Oxa09PHxRbPrL12AnPwYpBKXGA_8)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dcde13a9-fb2e-4fe3-ac71-ec0388c309db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The entire affair reveals a deeper truth about the governing philosophy behind DOGE. It rests on the childish Trump assumption that government can be understood as a collection of expenses rather than a collection of responsibilities. Under this theory, every line item appears suspicious, every expert appears expendable, and every safeguard appears unnecessary--until the moment it fails.
Then reality enters the room or the ranch.
Reality is entering now.
The irony is exquisite. The DOGE initiative, supposedly devoted to lowering costs, has now helped raise them. A project advertised as a crusade against waste is now forcing taxpayers to spend more. A Trump movement that promised managerial brilliance has only succeeded in demonstrating why experienced agricultural professionals were worried in the first place.

Insurify is a comparison platform that lets you check auto insurance quotes from multiple insurers in one place, side-by-side, in just a few minutes. Instead of manually visiting a dozen insurance websites, you answer a few questions once and quickly see what different companies may charge for similar coverage. [](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyskL2O4yAUhZ8Gd4m4QK6hoFgpSpdtt7Sw73WMhI0FbH7efuSp5gGm-6Rzzlecf_fhHmKK2-NvWNm395wHYopTaEzDxq-auDUuw2v5hMI1r2H7UIlPLrX-J-JtUFLhSeIJ8McSOvKjJAcde-gtoFb2gt3ix56C5QmdBEPg3IzjCOBwBmfCSH0X_SGUCAhWyos-ozHBOWmNmlCPrISRTLHlcm4LN36HOqdPfnI5T3ntkl9a26vQf4S6CXXbS248Naa8t5i3epSORN-C0Fcw9iIUTgdaqw6uIPS1K572V0wpVuyFkY81xPTtb7_50dOrrwAAAP__mZB-tw) And the differences can be surprisingly large. ---

| | | | | |
---
2026 McGovern Day

The turnout at this year's McGovern Day was historic, and the determined energy in the room was powerful. When we gather under George McGovern’s name, we are reminded that politics, at its best, is not about fame, power, or division. It is about service and courage. Government can improve people’s lives when it is guided by compassion, honesty, and common sense. South Dakotans feel that the government has fallen short of this expectation.

During my time as a legislator and community member, I’ve learned that South Dakotans feel that the government has fallen short of this expectation. Communities have expressed that the government isn’t working to address the issues that affect their daily lives. As governor, I will listen to every South Dakotan. Not just the people who agree with me. Not just the biggest donors or the loudest voices. Everyone.

It was an honor to speak on the same stage as Joe Biden, our excellent candidates, and local community leaders. We are in good company this election season, and I’m certain that together we can attain a better South Dakota.

| | | | |
---
Dell Rapids Meet and Greet

Nikki Gronli and I had a wonderful evening at our Dell Rapids meet and greet with a great crowd and many meaningful conversations. It was encouraging to visit with people from Dell Rapids, Colton, Colman, Garretson, and the surrounding communities about the issues that matter most to them. Our discussions covered everything from the challenges facing farmers to rising property taxes and the everyday affordability concerns impacting South Dakota families.

One issue that sparked a great deal of conversation was the high cost of childcare and its impact on families, our workforce, and the future of our communities. While local and state leaders have spent years discussing this challenge, there has been little action.

As governor, I will tackle this issue head-on by proposing a plan that uses existing dollars to provide childcare rebates for families and help make quality childcare more affordable for hardworking South Dakotans.

| | | |
---
| |
---
SIOUX FALLS PRIDE PARADE

Happy Pride Month. Seeing the outpour of support at this year’s Sioux Falls Pride Parade was reassuring, and shows that South Dakotans believe in a future that is inclusive and welcoming. This is the future that I will fight for.

Standing up for communities that feel ignored is a core facet of my priorities as governor. LGBTQ+ communities in South Dakota have long been actively attacked and ignored. This is another instance of unacceptable pressure that leads South Dakotans to leave home out of fear, alienation, and a lack of opportunity.

Our state shouldn’t be known for hatred and fear. “We the People” includes everyone. As governor, I will cultivate a South Dakota where every person in every community knows that they matter, and is treated with the dignity that they deserve.

| | |
---
| |
---
Pine Ridge Pow Wow

On Sunday, I had the opportunity to visit with OST President Frank Star Comes Out. He shared his frustrations with current leadership and the challenges facing the people of Pine Ridge.

For too long, decisions made in Pierre that directly impact our Tribal reservations have been made without meaningful consultation with Tribal leadership. That is not how a respectful government-to-government relationship should work.

As governor, I will work to rebuild trust and strengthen the relationship between the State of South Dakota and our Tribal Nations. Tribal leaders will be partners in the decisions that affect their communities. We must work together to address priorities like public safety, infrastructure, tourism, and economic development.

A stronger South Dakota depends on strong partnerships with every community in our state. I will listen and work diligently every day to earn the trust and respect of our Native brothers and sisters.

POLICY PERSPECTIVES

| |
---
Here’s the latest from across the campaign trail—key updates, major milestones, and where we’re headed next.

| | | |
---
| |
---
Affordable Housing

Housing affordability has a direct impact on opportunity and quality of life for all South Dakotans. It is a complex issue, and complex issues require creative solutions. We need a comprehensive approach that increases the supply of homes, supports first-time homebuyers, and gives communities long term assistance. As governor, I will work to expand workforce housing programs, support the construction of starter homes, and reduce unnecessary barriers that drive up building costs. I would also better utilize South Dakota's Governor's House Program, which has helped hundreds of families achieve homeownership while creating jobs and providing valuable workforce training. By modernizing and expanding the program, we can help more South Dakotans find an affordable path to owning a home.

Affordable housing is also an economic development issue. Businesses cannot find workers if workers cannot find a place to live. That's why I support targeted investments in infrastructure that open new areas for housing development, incentives for communities that create workforce housing opportunities, and programs that help young families achieve homeownership. Innovative partnerships between state government, local communities, employers, and housing developers ensures that affordable housing is available where it is needed most. By making housing more affordable, we can keep our young people in South Dakota, strengthen our small towns, and ensure that the next generation has the opportunity to build a future; right here at home.

| |
---
What’s Next.

Desserts with Democrats is on the 18th at Kuehn Park from 5:30–7:30 p.m. And, of course, I can’t miss Czech Days on the 19th in Tabor, South Dakota. If you would like to walk with my campaign in a parade, you can sign up using the “Volunteer!” button below. I hope to see you at any one of these great community events where connection is cultivated, and civic responsibility is grown.

Progress does not come from giving up when things get hard.

Join my grassroots campaign today.

name: Citizens for Amanda Pusczek
subject: What I heard at Shoals Pridefest
body:
Protecting our power and privacy
---
| | | | [ View in browser](https://nkkyj.r.ag.d.sendibm3.com/mk/mr/sh/SMJz09SDriOHTaiASW5eyDMeTo5R/1Pq8QW_ClOC5)
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
| | This past weekend, I had the incredible privilege of spending the day at Shoals Pridefest in Wilson Park. The unbreakable joy, solidarity, and resilience radiating from our LGBTQIA2S+ community across North Alabama was a powerful reminder of exactly why we are building this movement.
---
| | But as I stood at our campaign booth and listened to neighbors share their stories, a deeply concerning theme kept coming up: the rising anxiety over big-government intrusion into our private lives. From attacks on gender-affirming care to growing threats against IVF and reproductive freedom, the political establishment in Washington is obsessed with policing our bodily autonomy and violating basic medical privacy.
At the same time, we are seeing basic voting rights systematically eroded across the country. I spent time talking with young people who are working tirelessly to organize, register voters, and protect access to the ballot in a state that too often tries to silence them.
I will tell you exactly what I told them: **This is not a time to sit back and watch how things are happening.**
Now is when we must recognize our power and make change. Our community's right to live authentically, love freely, and make our own private medical decisions without political interference is entirely non-negotiable.
This rising generation of voters and organizers will chart the next era of our country and our world. As a frontline nurse running a 100% corporate PAC-free campaign, I will continue to unapologetically stand with, protect, and lift up these vital voices. I hope you will join me.
Thank you for staying in this fight and keeping our spirits high.
In solidarity,Amanda

| | Peter,
---
I'm going to be blunt with you.

We are closer to losing this country than most people are willing to admit.

Not someday. Not "if things keep going this way."

Right now.

And the scariest part?

It's not happening in Washington. It's happening in classrooms.

High schools. Colleges.

Places where the next generation is being shaped -- or more accurately... reshaped.

If you've ever looked at what's coming out of our schools and thought: _" What happened to this country?" _

You're not wrong. You're seeing it clearly.

Because while most people are arguing online... while they're hoping things will turn around... while they're waiting for the next election to fix everything...

The other side is doing something far more dangerous.

They're raising the next generation.

clean_body: The real frontline isn’t where you think | | | | | Peter, I'm going to be blunt with you. We are closer to losing this country than most people are willing to admit. Not someday. Not "if things keep going this way." Right now. And the scariest part? It's not happening in Washington. It's happening in classrooms. High schools. Colleges. Places where the next generation is being shaped -- or more accurately... reshaped. If you've ever looked at what's coming out of our schools and thought: " What happened to this country?" You're not wrong. You're seeing it clearly. Because while most people are arguing online... while they're hoping things will turn around... while they're waiting for the next election to fix everything... The other side is doing something far more dangerous. They're raising the next generation. Earlier. Faster. And with zero resistance in most places. That's how countries are lost. Slowly. Not in this environment. Not with the level of hostility these students face every single day. And yet... it's still happening. But Peter, here 's the part you need to understand: This is not a victory. It's a foothold. Because in the other 87% of schools? There is no resistance. None. Just one-sided propaganda from the Left. One-sided pressure on kids who are too young to even realize what's happening to them. That's the reality. The question isn't whether we're fighting. We are. The question is whether it's enough. Because right now, the students stepping up through Club America... They're not the majority. They 're the exception. They're the ones willing to take the heat. The ones willing to stand alone. The ones willing to risk being targeted just to say: " I love this country." And every time one of those students raises their hand... We have a choice. Back them. Or leave them on their own. Because when a student starts a chapter, we send them an activism kit -- with American flags. Pocket Constitutions. Leadership tools. Everything they need to actually stand their ground. Not symbolically. For real. They've already made the decision to lead. All they're waiting on... is you and me. Each activism kit costs $25. That 's it. $25 to make sure one student doesn't have to stand alone against the Left in a hostile school. $25 to put real tools in their hands. $25 to push back -- even if it's one campus at a time. But here's what gives me hope, Peter... Club America isn't slowing down. It's accelerating. Because every day, more students are stepping forward. Not because it's easy or popular... But because they know what 's at stake. They're starting chapters in schools where they were told not to. They're speaking truth in classrooms where the Left once went unchallenged. They're choosing courage in places designed to make them conform. And they're not alone. They're finding each other. They're bringing more students with them every day. They're building something real -- rooted in faith and freedom, grounded in truth, and unafraid to say that America is worth defending. That's how movements are built. Not from the top down... But from the ground up. One student. One school. One chapter at a time. And Peter -- that's exactly how we take this country back. But only if we move fast enough. Because the Left isn't slowing down. They're not taking a break. They're not afraid to push their anti-American ideas in every classroom they're in. And if we don't match that urgency... if we don't meet that moment with equal conviction... Then the generational window Charlie Kirk opened to save our country closes. And once it closes... It closes for good. That's what's at stake. Let's not waste this moment. Let's back our brave students -- while it still matters. | | For Charlie, Andrew Sypher Chief Field OfficerTurning Point USA P.S. I need you to hear this clearly... Charlie Kirk wasn't just dreaming big when he called me last year about Club America's progress. He was warning us: "The enemy is moving younger. They're coming after students earlier. We don 't have time to wait." And he was right. Look around. Club America may be in 13% of high schools... But in the other 87%? There is no pushback against the Left. No one telling those kids the truth. Just a Leftist pipeline -- from classroom... to belief... to voting booth. And once that pipeline is complete... It 's over. Peter, this is one of the last places a patriot like you can stop it before it 's too late to save our country. You may not be able to step into a hostile high school and stand for truth like these students do. But you can give critical support to a young freedom fighter who will. name: EON
subject: They turned off the lifeline for LGBTQ+ youth.
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
Peter - It's Pride Month. And I want to tell you something that's been weighing on me.
LGBTQ+ young people have called, texted, or chatted with the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline's dedicated LGBTQ+ line OVER 16 MILLION TIMES since it launched.
That equals thousands of contacts a day from kids in crisis — kids who needed someone on the other end of the line who understood what they were going through.
Then, the Trump administration shut it down. Even by the low standards of the MAGA Extremist party, this action was particularly cruel.
At a moment when nearly 40 percent of LGBTQ+ youth report seriously considering suicide in the past year, this administration looked at those kids and decided they didn't deserve a lifeline.
That’s why I had to spring into action.
I wrote the bill to fund this service. I led 104 of my colleagues in a bipartisan letter demanding it be protected. We passed the funding. And then this administration turned it off anyway.
This Pride Month, I'm asking you to help us fight back. Equal Opportunity Now exists to elect leaders who will stand up for every American — including the kids picking up the phone at their darkest moment and needing someone to answer.
Will you chip in $25 or $50 today to help us elect those leaders? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
DONATE NOW! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
Every young person deserves a shot. Every single one.
— Raja Krishnamoorthi
Visit Our Website To Learn More! [https://www.equalopportunitynow.org/]

Folks, can I explain something? I promise I'll be quick.

[ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133451320/627915417/-1473932214?refcode=logo&amount=10&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjZjQ4NDMwYy1iMDY5LWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=X8rd1IDAuqkbrwYu2yvf6zsytrrA4n4eMq0JHv2kHOA=) Folks, can I explain something? I promise I’ll be quick. As a kid, I was never “cool.” I was the skinny kid with Coke-bottle glasses and a funny last name. After that, I was a geologist. Then I got laid off, and we opened the state’s first brewpub — Wynkoop Brewing Company — in downtown Denver. I play the banjo. And I like to make corny jokes (personally, I think they’re hilarious). [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133451321/627915418/-502442095?amounts=5,10,15,25,50,100,250&refcode=email_061626_cool&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjZjQ4NDMwYy1iMDY5LWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=X8rd1IDAuqkbrwYu2yvf6zsytrrA4n4eMq0JHv2kHOA=) All of this is to say: **I’m not your typical politician.** To be quite honest, I only ever got into politics because I was sick and tired of corporate interests taking advantage of everyday Coloradans. The system has been rigged, and it still is. I ran for mayor, then governor, and eventually senator, always focusing on the same thing: putting Colorado families first and getting sh*t done. That’s why we do things a little differently around here. Instead of relying on corporate PACs to fund our campaign, we’re depending on folks like you to power our fight. body:

DEVELOPING... the Trump administration just sold off tens of thousands of acres of
the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge to oil and gas companies. He has promised to
“drill, baby, drill” from the extraordinary place the Gwich’in people call “the
sacred place where life begins.” We’re calling on our members for help. Sales like these have happened before, but there’s never been drilling in the
Arctic Refuge because the environmental movement has been able to break through
to major oil companies — and none of them bid on this recent lease sale.
Together, we’ve been able to hold the line in one of the last wild places on
Earth. Please, Peter: Renew your LCV membership for $15 during our Summer Membership Drive to TRIPLE your impact to protect irreplaceable wilderness like the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge >> https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/X6bzs~ LCV 2026 SUMMER MEMBERSHIP DRIVE

Match Status: TRIPLE MATCH ACTIVE >> https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/rNykfE~

Deadline: June 30, 2026
Membership Drive Goal: 5,000 membership contributions

Member Status: EXPIRED — renew your membership today for $15 >> https://links.messages.lcv. The Arctic National Wildlife Refuge is home to polar bears, millions of
migratory birds, and the porcupine caribou herd that has sustained the Gwich’in
people for generations. For decades, the Gwich’in have led the movement to keep
the Arctic Refuge free from corporate greed and extraction — no drilling, no
development. But Trump’s vision for the Refuge is clear: turn this sacred land into an industrial oil field. Here's the thing though: Trump can't force oil companies to drill the land. We need to remind these
companies that drilling in the Refuge is financially risky, wildly unpopular,
and incompatible with a rapidly changing Arctic. We need to keep organizing and keep public pressure up.That means supporting
Indigenous and frontline communities, holding oil companies and members of
Congress accountable, and registering as many pro-climate and pro-clean energy
voters as possible ahead of November’s midterm elections. But none of this works without you, Peter. We can’t afford to sit this
one out. RENEW YOUR MEMBERSHIP >> https://links.messages.lcv. Thank you for everything you do to protect public lands, Peter.
Together, we can make sure that Trump greed never breaks the ice in the Arctic
National Wildlife Refuge. America Fitzpatrick

| | This week, we celebrate 14 years of resilience and unbridled opportunity that define the **Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals** program, commonly known as **DACA.** America would not be where it is today without the bravery to be ambitious and to dream of opportunity and access. One of the many things that make America such a rich, beautiful nation is our long-held promise that, no matter where you come from, you, too, can take part in the American dream and deserve a realistic pathway to citizenship. Since DACA's establishment in 2012, the program has been a foundational pillar that has helped over **800,000** young people feel they belong and build careers that support themselves and their communities. **We cannot fall for the manufactured outrage and the vile lies directed at DACA and its recipients.** These are not the worst of the worst — they are some of our brightest minds, children who've lived here for the majority of their lives. The American dream is either true for all, or it is not true for anyone. For hundreds of thousands of people who've contributed so much to our country and built rich, fulfilling lives, the reality is that they are often made to feel unwelcome in the country they've called home for decades. We owe it to them and ourselves to right this wrong — my **Dignity Act** does just that. It seeks to provide a pathway to citizenship for DACA recipients. As we reflect on 14 years of resilience and opportunity that DACA has ushered in, my commitment to meaningful and comprehensive reform of our broken immigration system remains unwavering. clean_body: | | | | This week, we celebrate 14 years of resilience and unbridled opportunity that define the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals program, commonly known as DACA. America would not be where it is today without the bravery to be ambitious and to dream of opportunity and access. One of the many things that make America such a rich, beautiful nation is our long-held promise that, no matter where you come from, you, too, can take part in the American dream and deserve a realistic pathway to citizenship. Since DACA's establishment in 2012, the program has been a foundational pillar that has helped over 800,000 young people feel they belong and build careers that support themselves and their communities. We cannot fall for the manufactured outrage and the vile lies directed at DACA and its recipients. These are not the worst of the worst — they are some of our brightest minds, children who've lived here for the majority of their lives. The American dream is either true for all, or it is not true for anyone. For hundreds of thousands of people who've contributed so much to our country and built rich, fulfilling lives, the reality is that they are often made to feel unwelcome in the country they've called home for decades. We owe it to them and ourselves to right this wrong — my Dignity Act does just that. It seeks to provide a pathway to citizenship for DACA recipients. As we reflect on 14 years of resilience and opportunity that DACA has ushered in, my commitment to meaningful and comprehensive reform of our broken immigration system remains unwavering. * * *

| Fellow Patriot,

Ron Eller won the Republican primary.

And before the votes were even fully counted, the Democrat machine and Bennie Thompson were already making moves.

That is how much they want to keep this seat. Democrats in Congress know that if they lose Bennie Thompson's seat, they can't take back the House from Republicans. He has unlimited dark money, out-of-state donors, and a playbook designed to defeat Ron before November.

Here is what they are up against.

Ron is medical professional who has worked throughout central Mississippi. He is a former U.S. Army officer, small business owner, and supported by President Trump. He's against tax increases, wants to balance the federal budget, is the state leader of the term limits movement, protect our borders, and kick out the violent criminals and drug traffickers threatening our families.

President Trump has had enough of Bennie Thompson, and he knows he can count on Ron Eller's support in DC.

But none of that matters if we can't match the Democrats’ fundraising machine in this race.

Right now we need to show the country that Mississippi grassroots conservatives are ready to fight. A strong fundraising number this month tells Bennie Thompson and the DC Democrats that Mississippi is not for sale.

Will you chip in $10, $25, or whatever you can today to help Ron take on the Democrat machine this fall?

This is the race that could decide the House majority. Ron is the candidate who can win it.

Let's get to work.

body:
Represent your zip code at the GOP’s Midterm Convention...
| **__A Secure Briefing from the Desk of Jim Jordan__**
---
Peter,
---
I can’t lie to you, I’m deeply worried for our country...
---
**In special election after special election, Obama-funded Democrats have CRUSHED Republicans in voter turnout – and with just over 5 months to go until Election Day, Democrats are _still_ LEADING in all the generic ballot polls! **
---
But we still have time to turn the tide back in our favor.
---
I think in many ways this election is really two sentences: **_They're _crazy_. We're _not_._**
---
_Congressional Democrats have an abysmally low 18% approval rating because they want to open our borders, defund the police, indoctrinate our children, censor our free speech, and shred our constitutional rights._
---
However, that means NOTHING if we can’t motivate Republican voters to show up and cast a ballot when we need them most!
---
**Look – if we’re going to defy history and win the midterm elections, Republicans can’t just say we’re going to stop the Radical Left and call it a day.**
---
Instead, we have to give voters a reason to cast a ballot **_for_** the GOP, not merely **_against_** the Democrats!
---
What we need to do is contrast the Left’s insanity with our own common-sense platform that appeals to the vast majority of Americans, just like President Trump did during his historic victory in 2024.
---
That’s why the President announced that the GOP will be holding an unprecedented midterm convention!
---

Out of thousands of eligible voter records, I’ve chosen YOU to represent your zip code as an official **Virtual Grassroots Delegate** for our Midterm Convention based on your exemplary track record of supporting both President Trump and the Republican Party.

body:
| |
---
Hi friend, I wanted to follow up on Sue's email from yesterday because it gets at one of the biggest challenges we're facing right now. Sue shared how she wants to meet every Democratic voter in Rhode Island before the primary in just 84 days, and if you've spent any time around this campaign, you know she means it. She genuinely loves the conversations, the house parties, the community events, and hearing directly from people about what they want to see from their government. The people of Rhode Island are why she’s in this race! [**But the fact of the matter is: our team is running out of time to reach the voters of Rhode Island and let them know what makes Sue different than the rest of the candidates running. We’re going to be making decisions over the next few weeks about ad buys, mail, and all voter outreach. That’s why I’m checking in with you now: can you chip in just $25 to help us before time runs out?**](https://sue4ri.com/l/D51Msm5lfAzA) One thing I've learned as campaign manager is that when people meet Sue, they get excited. They see what's possible when someone spends their career advocating for and making real change happen — and are excited she decided to take that same approach statewide. We hear constantly that folks are tired of politicians who talk about problems and are excited because Sue will actually do something about it. **_The problem isn't building enthusiasm. The problem is making sure people have the opportunity to connect with her in the first place._** Unfortunately, there aren't enough hours in the day for Sue to personally knock on every door or attend every event across Rhode Island. (Trust me — she would if she could!) That's where ads and mail come in. They help us introduce Sue to voters who haven't met her yet and bring the conversations we're having in living rooms and community centers to people all across the state. Running a competitive statewide campaign takes resources, and we're at the point where every additional dollar helps us reach more voters with Sue's message. [**If you're able, will you make a contribution today and help us bring this campaign to every corner of Rhode Island? We know that it takes approximately $45 to reach 10 voters in Providence. So can you chip in $45 to help us reach 10 voters?**](https://sue4ri.com/l/7RqXWD6rZr9M)

And I know that when we secure our massive victory in November, it will all be thanks to smaller victories like this one. But just because we hit one goal doesn’t mean we can become complacent. We’re still running an incredibly competitive (and expensive) race in a battleground state. If we want to keep up the momentum, we need to keep our eyes on the road ahead. Our next deadline is a big one — an end-of-quarter deadline at the end of the month — and my team and I have set an ambitious goal: $75,000. Please, chip in with your first contribution of $20 today and help us meet our end-of-quarter goal. clean_body: I'm not blowing smoke | = I’m not blowing smoke when I say that the 2026 Midterm cycle is one of the most important slate of elections of my lifetime. With battlegrounds all across the country, you might be surprised to learn that I just can’t take my eyes off of Iowa. Seriously! The National Journal said Rob Sand “might be the strongest Democrat running statewide anywhere in the country this cycle,” and listed Iowa on their list of 10 most flippable governor’s races. My decades of experience are telling me the same thing. = | | = | = Recent polling shows Rob leading this race. And Cook Political Report just moved the race to a TOSS-UP. I don’t need to tell you what a big deal this is. The partisans running the show for the last decade have underfunded public schools, endangered folks’ health care, closed rural hospitals, and watched as jobs, opportunities, and people leave Iowa to go elsewhere. Look, we’ve been burned by Iowa before, but polling and on-the-ground sentiment is that Iowans are ready for something better. Rob Sand is the best candidate — and perhaps the only one — who can speak to the concerns of everyday Iowans, regardless of their political leanings. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation between Rob Sand and Fight Like Hell PAC will go through immediately: | = = | = = | = = Thanks, James Carville Fight Like Hell PAC PO BOX 15093 Lansing, MI 48901 United States ** | mailto:info@fightlikehellpac.org| | Paid for by Fight Like Hell PAC. body:
Wolf opponents ask federal officials to revisit Prop 114 after Keshel report challenges 2020 result
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi friends!
Want your full news breakdown? Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
_**FIRST UP, a special message from THE NICK SHIRLEY!**_
---
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
As Freedom Fest approaches, we've been asking ourselves an important question: _How can we ensure the people who have sacrificed the most for our country have the opportunity to be there?_
Today, we're excited to announce a new Freedom Fest initiative.
Over the last several days, generous supporters have stepped forward and offered to sponsor tickets for deserving individuals who may not otherwise be able to attend.
_**We're now accepting nominations for:**_ 🇺🇸 Gold Star Families 🇺🇸 Veterans 🇺🇸 Active Duty Military 🇺🇸 First Responders ...who would love to attend Freedom Fest but could use a little help getting there.
These men and women have sacrificed for our communities, our state, and our nation. We believe they deserve the opportunity to join us for this celebration of America's 250th Birthday and Colorado's 150th Birthday.
**Know Someone Who Should Be There? Reply to this email!**_A limited number of sponsored tickets will be available thanks to the generosity of donors who wanted to make sure Freedom Fest is accessible to those who have served._
_**Tickets now start at just $45.**_
**[June 26-27 | Douglas County Fairgrounds](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
🎟️ **[RMVFreedomFest.com](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
We'll see you there!
This is your Mountain Minute for Tuesday, June 16, 2026.
– Team RMV
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Wolf opponents ask federal officials to revisit Prop 114 after Keshel report challenges 2020 result](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
The fight over Colorado wolves has landed in a federal review process.
Opponents of wolf reintroduction are asking federal officials to reconsider Colorado’s wolf program after submitting a report that claims Proposition 114 did not actually pass.
Colorado Conservation Alliance filed the report June 5 with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service during a federal review of Colorado’s gray wolf program. Michael Clark, chairman of Colorado Conservation Alliance and CEO of Petrox Resources, signed the submission.
The filing takes aim at a message Clark says Coloradans have heard for years. “The message has been both constant and assertive, Colorado’s wolf program is ‘the will of the people’ because Proposition 114 passed,” Clark wrote to U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Director Brian Nesvik. Clark argues federal officials should take another look.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---

**Be part of history at Freedom Festival 2026.** Celebrate America’s 250th and Colorado’s 150th with with 2000+ patriots: two unforgettable days of speakers, action, community, and FUN for the whole family at the Douglas County Fairgrounds. _America only turns 250 once. Colorado only turns 150 once._ Secure your tickets now and be part of it.
[GET YOUR TICKETS NOW!](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
|
---
**[Lee Habeeb: “Storytelling is urgent work”](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* **Habeeb's worldview was shaped by an immigrant family that taught personal responsibility over victimhood:** his grandfather took him to naturalization ceremonies to witness American greatness, his mother's brother died fighting in France in WWII, and when heckled as the only kid with an Arabic last name in his New Jersey town, his parents refused to intervene — teaching him to handle things himself.
* **After co-founding The Laura Ingraham Show and spending two decades as VP of Content at Salem Media Group, Habeeb launched "Our American Stories" in 2016 — a nonprofit, politics-free show built on real Americans telling real stories:** now on nearly 500 stations with 1.2 million weekly listeners and 7 million podcast downloads in the past year, it reached #10 on Talkers Magazine's Heavy Hundred with zero marketing spend.
* **Habeeb sees storytelling as a patriotic duty:** tapped by the White House in 2025 to narrate John Adams' defense of British soldiers after the Boston Massacre for the America 250 series, he argues that remembering what previous generations did is the only way Americans can know who they are.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|

But through the lens of Jesus, Little Jack Horner tells a familiar story. Jack sees something he wants, reaches for it, takes it, and congratulates himself for getting it. That sounds a lot like us._

**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY JEN SCHUMANN | STATE | JUNE 12** _Every Coloradan who feels ignored at the Capitol can take comfort in this: they have not one but two people assigned to listen. Your House member splits attention among roughly 92,500 residents. Your senator, among about 171,800._
**[Eleven Colorado lawmakers on the ballot first reached office through appointment](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY JEN SCHUMANN | STATE | JUNE 11** _Every Coloradan who feels ignored at the Capitol can take comfort in this: they have not one but two people assigned to listen. Your House member splits attention among roughly 92,500 residents. Your senator, among about 171,800._

Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
When it comes to fighting voter suppression, our work is never done. Increasing participation in free and fair elections that are accessible to ALL eligible voters is our #1 goal for 2026, Team.
Unfortunately, this is what we're facing this year:
➜ Mail-in voting is under threat in state legislatures and now from the Supreme Court.
➜ Without vote-by-mail, millions of Americans will not be able to vote.
➜ With the 2026 midterm election around the corner, this is a disaster.
Remember, Team: Attacks on mail-in voting are voter suppression, plain and simple. We need your help now, more than ever. Will you chip in $35 to protect vote-by-mail before it’s too late? >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=061626_2&amount=35]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:

As voters across the country face unprecedented barriers at the ballot box , our fight to defend voting rights continues.
From educating voters on rapidly changing election laws -- like USPS changing the postmark rules -- to ensuring voters have the tools they need to make their voices heard this year, Voter Action Project will continue to stand strong in defense of voters in need, which is why we rely on early support from this team.
We have the momentum , but we have to keep doing the work to keep it going until November.
We’re working overtime to fight back and ensure every American can cast a ballot in 2026. Can you chip in $35 to support our work today? >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=061626_2&amount=35]

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.
Your support is crucial to our efforts. Will you donate today to help us protect voting rights? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/integrity-first-voter-action-project-1?refcode=061626_2&amount=20]

Now let me tell you why this mission means so much to me. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. Several years ago, I learned firsthand about the horrific reality of child trafficking. What I heard broke my heart. Children were being bought and sold.
Families were being torn apart.
Lives were being destroyed. **I couldn't forget it.** **I couldn't stay silent.** I kept asking myself one question: **"What if it were my child?"** That question changed my life. What started as a film project became a mission and a calling. That calling eventually led me to help produce the film _Sound of Freedom_. **Not for fame.**
**Not for awards.**
**But because I believed people needed to see the truth.** For years, many people said the film would never succeed. Doors closed.
Studios walked away.
People told us to give up. **But when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option.** And while the film helped awaken millions of people to this crisis, awareness alone is not enough. That is why we created the **Sound of Freedom Foundation**. Our mission is simple: **To stop the sale of God's children.**

With your help, we can overcome this obstacle and elect Democrats across the country this November.
#
Peter,
Across the country right now, there are incredible Democratic candidates running for office – up and down the entire ballot, in every single state.
They’ve got organizers knocking on doors. Volunteers making calls. These candidates are tirelessly showing up for their communities day after day.
The energy is there. The people are there.
**Money is the factor that is too often missing.**
**[ELECT DEMOCRATS: CHIP IN NOW](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/105313?refcode=em20260616-10577&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=10577%2E614464%2EIWoxx_)**
Here's the reality we’re facing right now: **The Republican Party is propped up by a network of billionaires and special interest groups who can write massive checks without giving it a second thought.** Dark money flows freely – funding attack ads, voter suppression efforts, and GOP candidates who answer to their donors instead of the people they were elected to serve.
**Democrats are doing things differently.** Our power comes from real people like you – grassroots donors who give what they can, when they can, because they believe that our country can do better than it’s doing right now.
And that matters enormously. But it also means we face hard choices.
**Right now, we’re working to support Democratic candidates in all 50 states.**
We all know there is no shortage of fights worth having – and no shortage of dedicated leaders who are ready to have them. But without adequate resources, we are forced to make impossible decisions about where to invest, which races to prioritize, and which communities we simply cannot reach.
**Every state matters. Every election matters. Every constituent matters.**
**[ELECT DEMOCRATS: CHIP IN NOW](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/105313?refcode=em20260616-10577&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=10577%2E614464%2EIWoxx_)**
We know what happens when Democrats show up everywhere: We win.
And we know what happens when we give up ground: Republicans entrench themselves for decades, gerrymander maps, restrict voting rights, and make it harder to fight back the next time. _We cannot afford to let that happen._
**If you've been waiting for the right moment to give – this is it.** Your donation today helps us support good candidates running in red and purple states across the country – where the odds are long but the stakes are even higher.
**[Will you chip in $5 or whatever you can to help us show up everywhere and WIN in 2026, Peter?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/105313?refcode=em20260616-10577&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=10577%2E614464%2EIWoxx_)**

Now it’s your turn! Send a letter to Congress today | | | Peter, did you know this was going on yesterday? June 15 marked 14 years of DACA, and thousands of our neighbors took action to call for a pathway to citizenship! [Will you join them?](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38pgfvzTEVjKf2pWpWyOhFqzdtMvQNOpEAId2R1v5_1RIE1hIWHrruBVGmCL-KU9gbAF8_TOcSFeoXq5WQu0I-DkJxUEy5On_ZxoHR0Tv217bwIpbfebFq5BpVtsGxMkbh0BpSc8ZOunQu012yPtuewu341BGWIGWzOi9-S1dQJbEA1T2QKUMFjSqESOtgu1OQdd3hkxR_OPxYz9571C0FGHDkBUi6T7D0P8hPKhsE-MT2HKXfB9tRI34CajYRPi4rOnqc0VDJFzt2T6ge3QGESCRMLAyJTG_4pzsFyzFQAq57UFqSOreCS1Bovh3BR0oE/4rj/1ivNa603SlGaaHfxzm8WZA/h0/h001.KRjm1Qznx7dx1pzfAPxGa_40ioTmKmX0unrPUDMSocw) Immigrant youth who were in high school when DACA was announced have now gone to college, started their careers, and built families in the only home they’ve ever known. **Even after all these years, their future is still up in the air.** DACA recipients are being targeted for detention and waiting months for their renewals to be processed. From DACA to TPS to asylum protections, our communities have had enough of watching this administration dismantle programs meant to protect us. We really couldn’t believe our eyes when we saw this report:

Political ad spending in Pennsylvania is expected to reach $381 MILLION in
this election cycle.

So Derek, if you’ve
ever wondered why we send out so many of these emails, well... that’s why.
It takes millions of dollars to win an election in a state like
Pennsylvania. And since that cash isn’t coming from Trump’s Mar-a-Lago
donors, we need it to come from folks like you.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/2026?t=1001&akid=76%2E245147%2EFUt9Ht ]Trust us, we know $5 doesn’t sound like a lot compared to $381 million.
But when you, your loved ones, and your neighbors all chip in, it adds up
quickly. Please, will you rush $5 or whatever you can to make sure we have
the resources to hold our own here in Pennsylvania?

Derek, if there is
any election in the entire country Donald Trump is paying attention to,
it’s this one. Here’s why:

Trump’s far-right movement can’t take control of the most competitive
battleground state in the country without winning this election. If Josh
Shapiro wins, he can veto any far-right attack on our fundamental freedoms
— on voting rights, abortion rights, and LGBTQ+ rights.

But if Trump’s hand-picked Republican nominee wins? There’s not much more
Trump needs to do.

Republicans already control every state-level office in Pennsylvania
besides Governor and Lieutenant Governor. They control one side of the
General Assembly too. So if we fall short on Election Day? Pennsylvania
will belong to Donald Trump... and Donald Trump alone.

But there’s one thing the far-right isn’t counting on,
Derek. And that’s you.

| Look at everything Trump and the Republican-controlled Senate have given us in the last 30 days
# [](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/61?t=1&akid=9869%2E5257348%2ECX42eH)
Derek, [**Before I ask you to make a contribution to our fight to retake the Senate majority,**](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1014?c0=q22026_abs_em.dQeZoR&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_GEN_GEN_AC90_20260616_PM1_V1_S1&email=&t=4&akid=9869%2E5257348%2ECX42eH) I want to take a step back for a moment — and look at everything Trump and the Republican-controlled Senate have given us in the last 30 days, and why allowing Republicans to maintain their majority is not an option. Here's what Republicans gave us: **The Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act.** The conservative majority effectively dismantled the last major legal protection against racial gerrymandering. Decades of civil rights progress, undone. And states are already moving to redraw maps before November, resulting in more Republican districts. **A UFC fight on the South Lawn of the White House**. A $60 million privately organized combat sports event — with VIP packages running into the millions, sponsorships in front of the White House and fighter weigh-ins staged at the Lincoln Memorial. **A $1.8 billion slush fund for Capitol rioters and cop beaters.** The Trump DOJ created an “anti-weaponization” fund — with no transparency, no oversight, and no application process yet defined — to make payments to the people who stormed the Capitol and assaulted police officers on January 6th on his behalf. Some are trying to claim up to $30 million in taxpayer money. **And prices keep going up.** Tariffs and the Iran War are hitting consumers directly. Inflation is the highest it’s been in 3 years. Groceries, gas, household goods — families are paying more for everything, and they know exactly who to thank. This is what one-party Republican corrupt rule looks like, Derek. Powered by People exists to help Democrats win big elections in Texas. And there is no bigger election this year than the one for U.S. Senate.
If James Talarico is going to be the first Democrat to win here since Lloyd Bentsen did in 1988; if he’s going to be the 51st vote in the Senate to fight corruption, bring down prices and stop Trump from destroying this country; if his victory will help us win other big races for Governor, Congress and the State House... then we’ve got to pull out all the stops.
That’s why, in addition to our successful statewide voter registration and voter turnout program on college campuses, we are now adding more innovative and yes, expensive, programs that give our volunteers new opportunities to connect with Texans who otherwise might not vote.
We have just partnered on a program that is mailing voter registration forms to hundreds of thousands of likely Democrats who have moved and have not yet updated their voter registration. Our volunteers are calling more than 130,000 of them to assist them in the process, to make sure they are able to legally vote at their new address and then offer to personally stay in touch with them to answer any follow up questions.
And — importantly! — our volunteers will stay in touch with them to ensure that they have the necessary reminders to cast their ballot and won’t stop reaching out until we’ve confirmed that they have voted.
I lost to Ted Cruz by a little more than 215,000 votes in 2018.
What if we’d had a program like this one back then? Imagine the hundreds of thousands of voters we could have reached and brought into that critical election.

body:
#
Peter, the hits are coming quick these days and it’s hard to keep track. To avoid wasting any more of your time than necessary, here are three good reasons you should chip in to VoteVets and help us elect a Democratic Congress this November.
1. The details for Trump’s “Iran Deal” have been released. With 13 Americans killed and up to $100 billion spent, Trump has agreed to pay Iran’s murderous regime $300 billion. There’s no nuclear deal on the books, and they control the Strait of Hormuz. The Art of the Deal.
2. Trump’s ballroom is going to cost $600 million, and internal documents from his own contractors indicate that $300 million of that is going to come from American taxpayers. As recently as last month, Trump said it was “a gift to the American people” that is “not going to be paid for by the taxpayer.” His words.
3. Trump has turned America’s 250th Independence Day celebration on the National Mall into his own partisan political rally. He is going to deliver one of his abusive, vitriolic, disgusting campaign speeches at an event that is meant to be above politics. He is out of control.

Trump’s doing all of this — acting like a king, ruling without dispute — because he knows Congress isn’t going to do anything about it. That’s the entire story of his presidency: Republicans kissing his ass when they should be holding him accountable.
In America’s 250th year, the most patriotic thing any of us can do is get Democrats elected to the House and Senate to stop him. If you have been waiting for the right time to get in the fight, this is it.

Peter,

I've spent decades fighting for conservative values.

I've known a lot of candidates. Very few actually deliver results.

Kurt Alme does.

Born and raised in Montana, Kurt loves this state. As U.S. Attorney, appointed by President Trump and confirmed twice by the Senate, he took on violent criminals, drug traffickers, and cartel networks threatening Montana families.

Under his leadership, criminal prosecutions hit a 20-year high to make communities safer.

That's not talk. That's action.
