_**by Lawrence Winnerman**_
## The Building
At 6:50 this morning, on a 206-acre cut of Caldwell County scrubland the permits call Project Snow, a twenty-six-year-old clipped into a scissor lift and began pulling cable through the steel skeleton of a building the public will never be allowed inside. The address is 1395 Bob White Road, outside Lockhart, thirty miles south of Austin. Two data centers, 380,000 square feet each, four hundred million dollars between them, broke ground this month. They will not power on until the fall of 2027. He is paid very well to wire them.
A thousand miles north, in Indianapolis, the Salesforce administrator from last month's roll call is awake too, refreshing a job board that has not changed since Tuesday. She is, in a way she will never be told, the reason the building exists. She will never see it.
He is wiring the machine that will run the software that finishes the job of replacing her.
They will never meet. In a heavy-overtime year he will clear something close to $150,000--more than the administrator ever made at the peak of a fourteen-year career, and he is twenty-six with no degree. But strip out the overtime and the per diem, the part of the check that disappears the day the roof goes on, and his base is roughly what hers was. The same four hundred million dollars lifts one of them and prices the other out of her profession. The difference between them is not the number. It is that he is at the beginning and she is at the end.
[If this is your first one--and for about a thousand of you it is--there was a tanker in the last installment, still offloading crude in the Houston Ship Channel, oil pumped before a war that had already moved the price](https://substack.com/redirect/498362b6-2b7e-4032-ba37-0a3e658f67dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). That tanker was the last cargo of the country we used to be. This building is the first structure of the one we are becoming.
One building. Two labor markets. One clock.
The rest of this essay is about the clock.
## The Two Reports
The May jobs report was good news, and the good news was real. Employers added 172,000 jobs--more than double the 80,000 economists expected. Unemployment held at 4.3 percent. March and April were revised up by a combined 93,000. Wages rose 3.4 percent over the year. The anchors said resilient. The president's account said booming. Every word of it can be defended, and that is exactly what makes it dangerous.
But if you read the report again, slower, and with an eye for details about where the jobs are coming from, it's different.
Leisure and hospitality: up 70,000, with restaurants and bars alone accounting for 48,000 of it--five times the sector's normal month, a spike some economists already suspect is World Cup hiring arriving ahead of the tournament. Local government: up 55,000. Health care: up 35,000, most of it home health and ambulatory care. **Carry the plate. Open the school. Turn the patient**. These are the jobs that cannot be done from a server farm and cannot be done by a model, and in May they were holding the headline up almost by themselves.
Now the other column. Financial activities lost 22,000 jobs in May and is down 107,000 from its peak a year ago. **White-collar payrolls** --the professional, managerial, information-economy work the administrator in Indianapolis spent fourteen years building toward--**have now contracted for thirty-one straight months**.
That's a recession. We are in a white-collar recession right now, and once again, only the AI datacenter building boom is hiding the truth.
Aaron Terrazas, the former Glassdoor economist who first counted the streak, says there is no precedent for it outside a recession going back seventy or eighty years; a white-collar sector shrinking while the overall economy keeps growing had never happened in the eighty-seven-year history of the data. The sectors that hire college graduates added an average of 49,000 jobs a month in the decade through early 2023. Since then they have been shedding 19,000 a month. Indeed's economists put it plainest: exactly half of the economy's sectors have lost jobs over the past year. **The headline is the average of the two halves.**
One report describes people serving the economy. The other describes people being removed from it. They were printed on the same page, under the same number, and only one of them made the air.
On June 9, _**Axios**_ looked at all of it and ran the sentence this entire essay exists to take apart: "White-collar jobs are under pressure, but the labor market is fine."
The labor market is fine the way a fever patient is fine--if you only take the temperature in the one place that isn't hot.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.2iP6b7x12AmiQ1YjpHjtoAhotUuW_w4BecJjBnAKntc?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=202346829)
## The Door
Here is the number that should have led every broadcast, and didn't lead even one: 3.2 percent. That is the hiring rate--the share of jobs that are actually filled in a month, not posted, filled. It is among the lowest in thirteen years, a level the economy last saw around 2013, when unemployment was close to 7.5 percent, nearly twice what it is now. Think about what that means: the door into work is as narrow as it was in the wreckage of the last recession. The only reason the line outside it looks shorter is that fewer people are being moved through it in either direction--fired or hired.
And then, two weeks before the May report, the objection arrived right on schedule. In April, job openings jumped to 7.6 million, the biggest one-month rise since 2021, and almost all of it--668,000 postings--came from exactly the professional and business services that have been bleeding for two and a half years. The headline wrote itself: White-collar hiring is back.
_**It isn 't. **_

Only one of them is good news. | | and | Jun 16| | | ∙| | Preview ---|---|--- | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- | | ---|---|--- by Lawrence Winnerman The Building At 6:50 this morning, on a 206-acre cut of Caldwell County scrubland the permits call Project Snow, a twenty-six-year-old clipped into a scissor lift and began pulling cable through the steel skeleton of a building the public will never be allowed inside. The address is 1395 Bob White Road, outside Lockhart, thirty miles south of Austin. Two data centers, 380,000 square feet each, four hundred million dollars between them, broke ground this month. They will not power on until the fall of 2027. He is paid very well to wire them. A thousand miles north, in Indianapolis, the Salesforce administrator from last month's roll call is awake too, refreshing a job board that has not changed since Tuesday. She is, in a way she will never be told, the reason the building exists. She will never see it. He is wiring the machine that will run the software that finishes the job of replacing her. They will never meet. In a heavy-overtime year he will clear something close to $150,000--more than the administrator ever made at the peak of a fourteen-year career, and he is twenty-six with no degree. But strip out the overtime and the per diem, the part of the check that disappears the day the roof goes on, and his base is roughly what hers was. The same four hundred million dollars lifts one of them and prices the other out of her profession. The difference between them is not the number. It is that he is at the beginning and she is at the end. . That tanker was the last cargo of the country we used to be. This building is the first structure of the one we are becoming. One building. Two labor markets. One clock. The rest of this essay is about the clock. The Two Reports The May jobs report was good news, and the good news was real. Employers added 172,000 jobs--more than double the 80,000 economists expected. Unemployment held at 4.3 percent. March and April were revised up by a combined 93,000. Wages rose 3.4 percent over the year. The anchors said resilient. The president's account said booming. Every word of it can be defended, and that is exactly what makes it dangerous. But if you read the report again, slower, and with an eye for details about where the jobs are coming from, it's different. Leisure and hospitality: up 70,000, with restaurants and bars alone accounting for 48,000 of it--five times the sector's normal month, a spike some economists already suspect is World Cup hiring arriving ahead of the tournament. Local government: up 55,000. Health care: up 35,000, most of it home health and ambulatory care. Carry the plate. Open the school. Turn the patient. These are the jobs that cannot be done from a server farm and cannot be done by a model, and in May they were holding the headline up almost by themselves. Now the other column. Financial activities lost 22,000 jobs in May and is down 107,000 from its peak a year ago. White-collar payrolls --the professional, managerial, information-economy work the administrator in Indianapolis spent fourteen years building toward--have now contracted for thirty-one straight months. That's a recession. We are in a white-collar recession right now, and once again, only the AI datacenter building boom is hiding the truth. Aaron Terrazas, the former Glassdoor economist who first counted the streak, says there is no precedent for it outside a recession going back seventy or eighty years; a white-collar sector shrinking while the overall economy keeps growing had never happened in the eighty-seven-year history of the data. The sectors that hire college graduates added an average of 49,000 jobs a month in the decade through early 2023. Since then they have been shedding 19,000 a month. Indeed's economists put it plainest: exactly half of the economy's sectors have lost jobs over the past year. The headline is the average of the two halves. One report describes people serving the economy. The other describes people being removed from it. They were printed on the same page, under the same number, and only one of them made the air. On June 9, Axios looked at all of it and ran the sentence this entire essay exists to take apart: "White-collar jobs are under pressure, but the labor market is fine." The labor market is fine the way a fever patient is fine--if you only take the temperature in the one place that isn't hot. The Door Here is the number that should have led every broadcast, and didn't lead even one: 3.2 percent. That is the hiring rate--the share of jobs that are actually filled in a month, not posted, filled. It is among the lowest in thirteen years, a level the economy last saw around 2013, when unemployment was close to 7.5 percent, nearly twice what it is now. Think about what that means: the door into work is as narrow as it was in the wreckage of the last recession. The only reason the line outside it looks shorter is that fewer people are being moved through it in either direction--fired or hired. And then, two weeks before the May report, the objection arrived right on schedule. In April, job openings jumped to 7.6 million, the biggest one-month rise since 2021, and almost all of it--668,000 postings--came from exactly the professional and business services that have been bleeding for two and a half years. The headline wrote itself: White-collar hiring is back. It isn 't. | | ---|---|--- Continue reading this post for free in the Substack app | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Cliff Schecter PO Box 8384, Cincinnati, OH 45208 ? ?

Dear Patriot, They're trying to put an innocent cop in prison for **life**. Why? For defending himself against a fleeing suspect who dragged him with a car. I've been in law enforcement for decades. I've seen the system abused. But what is happening to Officer James Brennand of San Antonio, Texas makes my blood boil, and it should make yours boil too. While millions of Americans struggle to make ends meet during a brutal affordability crisis, Donald Trump has a new priority for the federal government: building a 250-foot monumental arch in Washington, D.C.
Just as this past weekend’s MMA fight was supposedly about America’s 250th birthday, but coincidentally was held on Donald Trump’s own 80th birthday, this arch has nothing to do with the American people. And Trump admits it!
When a journalist asked who the arch was for, Trump answered with one word: “Me.”
This project is completely absurd — and unlawful.
Trump is bypassing congressional approval and disregarding legal procedures. So as we have done many times before when the President violates the law — we’re taking action. Today I filed an amicus brief in federal court along with a coalition of more than a dozen other attorneys general to challenge the Trump administration's failure to follow the law.
If Donald Trump wants to use taxpayer dollars to build a giant monument to himself, he certainly can’t be allowed to bypass legal procedures in the process. Add your name today. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/Y6TnWgnQ5U25XRFpaFy3UA2]

Besides being a ridiculous vanity project, the arch will also pose a hazard to air travel, increase traffic, and disrupt the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery, where more than 400,000 service members, veterans, and military family members are laid to rest.
This President violates the law so brazenly and so consistently that it’s clear he believes he’s untouchable. But Trump is not a king — and we’ve proven that with the law on our side, we can win these fights.
Thanks for reading and speaking out with me.
—Rob

clean_body: | = Friend, it’s Jane. I’m coming to you with a quick, time-sensitive request. We’re just a few hours away from our mid-month deadline, and we cannot afford to fall short of this one. Now that so many of our endorsed candidates have made it through their primaries, they’re facing grueling fights all the way to Election Day — fights where Big Oil and their allies will pour millions into attacks, misinformation, and anything else they can use to stop climate champions from winning. So I am turning to you, while there’s still time to make a difference.= | = After 88 years on this Earth, I’ve learned: Nothing scares bullies and corporate polluters more than people power. Let me explain why. Every victory we’ve had since I started the Jane Fonda Climate PAC — from electing over 240 climate leaders nationwide to flipping over 20 seats last year — has come from our collective power. So when I tell you that we’re creating better, one person, one action, one voter at a time,believe me. You, friend, are powering the change that could save us and our planet. = = Change doesn’t just happen overnight. It takes each and every one of us investing in these candidates as early as we can to give them the strategic advantage they need over their corporate-backed opponents. Thank you for everything you do. In solidarity, Jane xx = | = | = = Follow along: | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|--- Paid for by Jane Fonda Climate PAC, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee. Peter, Our democracy is being dismantled by those who are desperate to hold on to power. Republican state lawmakers and unbalanced judiciaries constraining only one political party have aided and abetted Donald Trump's plan to deny people their right to choose their government. **They’ve shown they’re willing to silence voters, especially those in Black and Latino communities.** Defeating this current wave of racial and partisan gerrymandering requires abandoning outdated playbooks. That’s exactly why we have a rigorous, multi-front strategic plan to defeat Trump’s gerrymandering and protect democracy. It starts in DEFEND states, fighting back wherever Republicans have passed — or will try to pass — new gerrymanders. It requires going on offense, too, empowering voters in COUNTER states to pass counter-measures to level the playing field. And here’s the final, critical pillar: **Build a firewall for fairness in ADVANCE states with success at the ballot box.** [**Setting a plan of this scale in motion requires uncompromising resistance and unprecedented mobilization. * **Win democratic trifectas** (the governor and majorities in both houses of the legislature) in states like Wisconsin to set the stage for a map-drawing effort to counter the Republican gerrymanders.

name: Amy Friedman, Campaign Manager
subject: Important memo on the Texas governor’s race
body:
The environment is here for Texas Democrats. Now we need the resources to match it.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Hi Peter. It's Amy, Gina’s campaign manager.
I want you to read something. I put together a memo on where this race actually stands — because I think a lot of national Democrats don’t have the full picture yet.
The short version: Greg Abbott is more vulnerable than he’s ever been, and Gina is building exactly the coalition that wins this race. But Abbott has $106 million and he’s planning to spend it to paper over his record and stop us from taking back Texas. We need the resources to fight back.
**[Read the memo. Or if you don’t need convincing, pitch in what you can now.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20260616_2_memo.iNpAvy&refcode=em20260616-1351&t=1&akid=1351%2E299639%2EPoRnrY)**
[Donate »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260616_2_memo.sWNsq7&amount=5&refcode=em20260616-1351&t=2&akid=1351%2E299639%2EPoRnrY)
=============================================================
**SUMMER 2026 CAMPAIGN MEMO ON TX-GOV**
**FROM:** Amy Friedman, Campaign Manager, Gina for Texas
**TO:** Interested Parties
Let me tell you exactly where our race stands, and why the next few months are going to determine whether this is the year we take Texas back.

The Texas governor’s race has been in single digits for months, and it still isn’t getting the attention it deserves from national Democrats.
**The polls tell a consistent story: Abbott is in the weakest position of his career.**
* Recent polls confirm this race is closing fast:
* Texas Public Opinion Research (April 2026): Abbott 48–Gina 43, with Gina winning independents by 13, moderates by 32, and Latino voters by 22
* Somos Votantes (April 2026): Gina leads with Latino voters statewide
* A PPP survey found Gina tied with Abbott 48-48 in TX-23, a district Trump carried by 15 points.
* A three-term incumbent who cannot break 50% in any publicly released poll is an incumbent in trouble.

**Abbott’s war chest is a real threat — and it’s built on corruption**
* Greg Abbott entered 2026 with $105.7 million on hand. Nine figures.
* He didn’t build this by winning over working Texans. His top donors include oil executives, private prison owners, and data center developers — at a time when data centers are threatening to spike Texas utility bills.
* This is what pay-to-play governance looks like. Abbott has handed out $1 billion in no-bid contracts to his donors. He rammed through a $1 billion school voucher scam after receiving the largest campaign contribution in Texas history from an out-of-state billionaire.
* The Greg Abbott Corruption Tax is real — and Texans are paying it every time their utility bill, property tax, or grocery receipt arrives.

**After 12 years in power, Greg Abbott owns Texas’s problems — and they are serious.**
* Texas has the highest uninsured rate in the country (for adults and for children).
* More than one million Texas kids lack health coverage, and it’s getting worse.
* Abbott has refused Medicaid expansion for over a decade, leaving hundreds of thousands of Texans without coverage and billions of federal dollars on the table.
* Property taxes have increased 75% under Abbott. Texans pay the highest property tax burden in the state’s history. Abbott has said for years he’ll fix it. But it keeps getting worse.
* Abbott held public school funding hostage in 2023, refusing to fund classrooms unless the Legislature passed his voucher scam. School districts across the state have had to lay off staff, cut programs, and close schools as a result.
* Texas has had more major power outages than any other state. The grid failed in 2021, killing Texans. Abbott promised it was fixed, but problems persist.

**Gina has built something real — but we need more resources to carry her message forward.**
* Gina is running a people-powered campaign. Her average donation is under $50.
* She is winning key demographics: independents by 13, moderates by 32, Black voters by 57, Latino voters by 22, and voters 18-24 by 49.
* Gina is tied with Abbott in a Trump +15 district. She is cutting into Abbott’s base. It’s a sign she’s genuinely connecting.
* But $106 million is a lot of money. When that money hits the airwaves across the state, we’re going to need real resources to fight back.

**Texas Democrats are positioned to win.**
* All the warning signs are flashing for Republicans – not only are they trailing in polling, but they are losing special elections left and right this year in historically deep red areas of Texas, where Democrats are turning out to flip school board seats, county commissions, and state Senate seats too.
* For the first time in years, Texas Democrats have candidates at the top of the ticket with real momentum in both the governor’s race and the U.S. Senate race:
* Gina is closing the gap in a state that hasn’t elected a Democratic governor for 30 years. Talarico has a small edge in the Senate race. The environment is here. Texas has a very strong Democratic ticket. Now we just need the investment to match it.

**The bottom line.**
* Greg Abbott is scared. He’s told his own donors he’s at real risk of losing seats statewide. His approval is at a career low.
* The coalition Gina is assembling: Latino voters, young voters, independents, moderates, working families across every corner of Texas — is the coalition that will win this race.
* This is Democrats’ best chance in 25 years to take back Texas. The coalition is here, the candidates are out front, working hard to carry their message to every voter. The environment is favorable. What determines whether we win is whether national Democrats decide Texas is worth the investment.
* **We can win this race if we all show up.**

=============================================================
Peter, I see the internal numbers, I hear from our organizers on the ground, I watch what’s happening with voters in every corner of this state. I know what this race looks like, and I’m telling you: We can win.
But not without you. Abbott is preparing to unleash his $106 million war chest. We need to be ready.
[**Will you rush a donation to Gina right now?** ](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20260616_2_memo.iNpAvy&refcode=em20260616-1351&t=3&akid=1351%2E299639%2EPoRnrY)

Thank you for being part of our campaign.
– Amy Friedman, Campaign Manager, Gina for Texas

He rammed through a $1 billion school voucher scam after receiving the largest campaign contribution in Texas history from an out-of-state billionaire. The Greg Abbott Corruption Tax is real — and Texans are paying it every time their utility bill, property tax, or grocery receipt arrives. After 12 years in power, Greg Abbott owns Texas’s problems — and they are serious. Texas has the highest uninsured rate in the country (for adults and for children). More than one million Texas kids lack health coverage, and it’s getting worse. Abbott has refused Medicaid expansion for over a decade, leaving hundreds of thousands of Texans without coverage and billions of federal dollars on the table. Property taxes have increased 75% under Abbott. Texans pay the highest property tax burden in the state’s history. Abbott has said for years he’ll fix it. But it keeps getting worse. Abbott held public school funding hostage in 2023, refusing to fund classrooms unless the Legislature passed his voucher scam. School districts across the state have had to lay off staff, cut programs, and close schools as a result. Texas has had more major power outages than any other state. The grid failed in 2021, killing Texans. Abbott promised it was fixed, but problems persist. Gina has built something real — but we need more resources to carry her message forward. Gina is running a people-powered campaign. Her average donation is under $50. She is winning key demographics: independents by 13, moderates by 32, Black voters by 57, Latino voters by 22, and voters 18-24 by 49. Gina is tied with Abbott in a Trump +15 district. She is cutting into Abbott’s base. It’s a sign she’s genuinely connecting. But $106 million is a lot of money. When that money hits the airwaves across the state, we’re going to need real resources to fight back. Texas Democrats are positioned to win. All the warning signs are flashing for Republicans – not only are they trailing in polling, but they are losing special elections left and right this year in historically deep red areas of Texas, where Democrats are turning out to flip school board seats, county commissions, and state Senate seats too. For the first time in years, Texas Democrats have candidates at the top of the ticket with real momentum in both the governor’s race and the U.S. Senate race: Gina is closing the gap in a state that hasn’t elected a Democratic governor for 30 years. Talarico has a small edge in the Senate race. The environment is here. Texas has a very strong Democratic ticket. Now we just need the investment to match it. The bottom line. Greg Abbott is scared. He’s told his own donors he’s at real risk of losing seats statewide. His approval is at a career low. The coalition Gina is assembling: Latino voters, young voters, independents, moderates, working families across every corner of Texas — is the coalition that will win this race. This is Democrats’ best chance in 25 years to take back Texas. The coalition is here, the candidates are out front, working hard to carry their message to every voter. The environment is favorable. What determines whether we win is whether national Democrats decide Texas is worth the investment. We can win this race if we all show up. ============================================================= Peter, I see the internal numbers, I hear from our organizers on the ground, I watch what’s happening with voters in every corner of this state. I know what this race looks like, and I’m telling you: We can win. But not without you. Abbott is preparing to unleash his $106 million war chest. We need to be ready. Thank you for being part of our campaign. – Amy Friedman, Campaign Manager, Gina for Texas Email us: mailto:info@ginafortexas.com

Trump wants his own personal defense attorney at the helm of the Department of Justice. | |

Peter, Donald Trump has nominated Todd Blanche to be Attorney General of the United States. **It’s one of his most self-dealing picks yet.** Blanche was actually Trump’s personal criminal defense lawyer before becoming Acting Attorney General. But his time at the Department of Justice has proven that he’s still working for his former boss, not the American people. Under his leadership, the DOJ has gone after Trump’s enemies, including former FBI Director James Comey and the Southern Poverty Law Center. The DOJ also majorly botched the release of the Epstein files, exposing the names of survivors. And he’s behind the $1.8 billion slush fund to pay out Trump’s political allies. **The office of the Attorney General is supposed to work on behalf of the people, not a wannabe dictator. But like the rest of our political system, wealthy extremists are now capturing and rigging the Department of Justice.** A simple majority in the Senate is required in order to confirm Blanche. That means just four Republican "no" votes can stop him. [**More than four Republicans have broken with Trump and Blanche before. We've seen a declining birth rate since the 1970s. Fewer kids mean fewer workers down the road paying into the system that supports our seniors. Today, we have a large aging population--Baby Boomers retiring, living longer, and relying on Social Security. The worker-to-beneficiary ratio is shrinking, putting real pressure on the program that so many Americans depend on.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/348e8e8c-25c5-4f55-affc-2837bc1c7b06?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Now layer on the explosion of data centers. These massive facilities are popping up across our country. They bring investment and economic activity-- construction jobs, tax revenue during build-out, and yes, a few permanent roles. But here's the big picture that too few are talking about: data centers are replacing traditional jobs that paid into Social Security through payroll taxes.
Many data centers run with a skeleton crew, replacing thousands of jobs with just dozens. They are efficient for companies, but they pull income away from the system that supports our retirees.
[Subscribe](https://substack..u--KGdrQ1Esb7kDtj-7Fw201KWEa-uG2tYoBkGerHEQ?)
We don't have to be anti-progress. America needs to build the economy of the future to stay on top. Data centers can bring opportunities, especially if we tie incentives to infrastructure upgrades and energy reliability without hiking rates on families. But we can't let them hollow out the funding for Social Security.
**A Common-Sense Solution**
Use the massive revenue and economic activity from data centers to help shore up Social Security. Let's make sure the gains from the digital economy support the workers and retirees who built America.
It's up to us to push our elected leaders to do the right thing. Write your elected representatives. Have them commit to real solutions to save Social Security.
**The fight for a better future starts now.**

clean_body: We've seen a declining birth rate since the 1970s. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more | | | Jun 16 | | | | | | | | | | | | We've seen a declining birth rate since the 1970s. Fewer kids mean fewer workers down the road paying into the system that supports our seniors. Today, we have a large aging population--Baby Boomers retiring, living longer, and relying on Social Security. The worker-to-beneficiary ratio is shrinking, putting real pressure on the program that so many Americans depend on. | | ---|---|--- Now layer on the explosion of data centers. These massive facilities are popping up across our country. They bring investment and economic activity-- construction jobs, tax revenue during build-out, and yes, a few permanent roles. But here's the big picture that too few are talking about: data centers are replacing traditional jobs that paid into Social Security through payroll taxes. Many data centers run with a skeleton crew, replacing thousands of jobs with just dozens. They are efficient for companies, but they pull income away from the system that supports our retirees. ? We don't have to be anti-progress. America needs to build the economy of the future to stay on top. Data centers can bring opportunities, especially if we tie incentives to infrastructure upgrades and energy reliability without hiking rates on families. But we can't let them hollow out the funding for Social Security. A Common-Sense Solution Use the massive revenue and economic activity from data centers to help shore up Social Security. Let's make sure the gains from the digital economy support the workers and retirees who built America. It's up to us to push our elected leaders to do the right thing. Write your elected representatives. Have them commit to real solutions to save Social Security. The fight for a better future starts now. Thank y'all for reading, Kyle ? | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Kyle Sweetser 548 Market Street PMB 72296, San Francisco, CA 94104 ? ?

I promise there is a positive takeaway from this message. First, a memory: I worked as an intern in a federal prosecutor's office, and I always found it funny that the break room had the above poster from _Tombstone_ , presumably because of the tagline. It was motivating for those of us who believed justice really was coming. This was during the Bush administration, but there was truly no way to tell whether a Democrat or Republican was in charge at the ground level. The work spoke for itself.
I think we all know that's not true today. Consider what has been revealed about the DOJ in the stunning [investigation](https://substack.com/redirect/7de6b50a-9b5d-46c4-a8e2-00ca3e79b6b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from today's New York Times showing how RFK Jr. received _**$1 million dollars**_ from a company selling kratom, an opioid-like drug available in gas stations. WHY IS A CABINET SECRETARY ALLOWED TO ACCEPT ONE MILLION DOLLARS FROM ANYONE, FOR ANY REASON, I want to scream from the rooftops. (The article says it went to his PAC, but still. Why does he have a PAC?). Especially when the company's CEO did prison time for fraud!
Needless to say, the DOJ is not investigating Kennedy, even though the article documents how he got the money after pressuring the governor of Ohio to drop a proposed kratom ban. In fact, DOJ somehow saw the issue the same way and dropped its own investigation into the safety of this company's kratom. And the cherry on top is that an investor in the company is none other than Secretary Markwayne Mullin, whose stake may be as much as $1 million. Obviously he stands to benefit, and the article discusses how he used his own influence accordingly.
I suppose someone could ask, do million-dollar instances of corruption even warrant federal resources in a world where the Trump family's corruption is so far into the [billions](https://substack.com/redirect/baaa3973-c6dd-4c29-827c-2cf8bb376cc3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)? Of course they do. Kratom has been associated with a wave of [deaths](https://substack.com/redirect/cc5aea10-85eb-4e2e-a55e-1443c69651ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). I've sat with families who lost people to drugs. It matters immensely if our public officials are being paid to allow drug distribution on a larger and even more unsafe scale.
Here is the positive side that I promised: there truly is something we can do about this. But the next Democratic administration will have to innovate. The approach of appointing a single, eminent prosecutor to deal with all of this corruption will not work, in part because the supposedly-eminent often can't or won't communicate with the public, and probably also because our society doesn't agree much on eminence anymore.
The new approach will have to be analogous to what the Marines call a "combined arms" exercise. State-level prosecutions and private civil litigation will become critical avenues if Trump issues blanket pardons, since those could complicate federal prosecutions. And don't forget that a Democratic House majority from 2027-2029 can probably develop evidence before any future criminal investigation would begin. The administration will stonewall them, of course, but banks and communications companies, and witnesses who are out of government, may not be able to withhold their evidence as easily. That's an important head start.
So if you find yourself questioning whether retaking the House majority actually matters against corruption of this scale, take it from me that the answer is yes. It's not the whole ballgame, but it's a vital and practical first step. After that, many of us will have to work together across multiple fronts for many years. But what choice is there? Our form of government rests on people believing, to some degree, that their vote makes a difference. Corruption is uniquely capable of destroying that.
Here in Pennsylvania, there are at least four congressional seats that we believe can be flipped, based on our excellent candidates and the dynamics shaping up this year. You can take action right now to support all four of these candidates:
* [Bob Harvie](https://substack.com/redirect/929ec919-e557-4d29-acd2-2202cd1f8f5b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* [Paige Cognetti](https://substack.com/redirect/450fbaa0-2b5c-4da5-a512-de5a1c8213de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

First, a memory: I worked as an intern in a federal prosecutor's office, and I always found it funny that the break room had the above poster from Tombstone , presumably because of the tagline. It was motivating for those of us who believed justice really was coming. This was during the Bush administration, but there was truly no way to tell whether a Democrat or Republican was in charge at the ground level. The work spoke for itself. I think we all know that's not true today. Consider what has been revealed about the DOJ in the stunning from today's New York Times showing how RFK Jr. received $1 million dollars from a company selling kratom, an opioid-like drug available in gas stations. WHY IS A CABINET SECRETARY ALLOWED TO ACCEPT ONE MILLION DOLLARS FROM ANYONE, FOR ANY REASON, I want to scream from the rooftops. (The article says it went to his PAC, but still. Why does he have a PAC?). Especially when the company's CEO did prison time for fraud! Needless to say, the DOJ is not investigating Kennedy, even though the article documents how he got the money after pressuring the governor of Ohio to drop a proposed kratom ban. In fact, DOJ somehow saw the issue the same way and dropped its own investigation into the safety of this company's kratom. And the cherry on top is that an investor in the company is none other than Secretary Markwayne Mullin, whose stake may be as much as $1 million. Obviously he stands to benefit, and the article discusses how he used his own influence accordingly. I suppose someone could ask, do million-dollar instances of corruption even warrant federal resources in a world where the Trump family's corruption is so far into the ? Of course they do. Kratom has been associated with a wave of . I've sat with families who lost people to drugs. It matters immensely if our public officials are being paid to allow drug distribution on a larger and even more unsafe scale. Here is the positive side that I promised: there truly is something we can do about this. But the next Democratic administration will have to innovate. The approach of appointing a single, eminent prosecutor to deal with all of this corruption will not work, in part because the supposedly-eminent often can't or won't communicate with the public, and probably also because our society doesn't agree much on eminence anymore. The new approach will have to be analogous to what the Marines call a "combined arms" exercise. State-level prosecutions and private civil litigation will become critical avenues if Trump issues blanket pardons, since those could complicate federal prosecutions. And don't forget that a Democratic House majority from 2027-2029 can probably develop evidence before any future criminal investigation would begin. The administration will stonewall them, of course, but banks and communications companies, and witnesses who are out of government, may not be able to withhold their evidence as easily. That's an important head start. So if you find yourself questioning whether retaking the House majority actually matters against corruption of this scale, take it from me that the answer is yes. It's not the whole ballgame, but it's a vital and practical first step. After that, many of us will have to work together across multiple fronts for many years. But what choice is there? Our form of government rests on people believing, to some degree, that their vote makes a difference. Corruption is uniquely capable of destroying that. Here in Pennsylvania, there are at least four congressional seats that we believe can be flipped, based on our excellent candidates and the dynamics shaping up this year. You can take action right now to support all four of these candidates: Justice is coming! Conor Lamb is free today. But if you enjoyed this post, you can tell Conor Lamb that their writing is valuable by pledging a future subscription. That’s why we need your support right now to make sure every one of these incredible leaders can finish their campaigns strong and win on Tuesday.

name: Sheriff Joe Arpaio
subject: They charged him with a felony for stopping a riot
body:
Dear Patriot,
They charged a cop with a felony for stopping a riot. I am not making this up.
They want to lock him away for using **non-lethal bean bag rounds** against a violent mob that was blocking an interstate highway, hurling rocks at officers, and bringing Molotov cocktails to the party.
I have seen a lot in my years in law enforcement. I have seen politics poison the justice system. But what is being done to Officer Jeffrey Teng of Austin, Texas is one of the most shameless, stomach-turning betrayals of law enforcement I have ever witnessed.
** [It has to stop — and I need your help to stop it.](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=7ae7a47bc5df4e03993605de9de93006&_e=hDALp-jb2BWyYFmIy8MLPSd2OtCsPmB2Krf5i8yUUaxP2J2neHCXDqgLpeOBJONiP477B7595Y3GJITCIUUFswa5RvwReuyk_gBKaRj0sm4KqNIHUsYIpdwnpk3IYC4TI7q2sMNf1E2hSCRoCOK8retNu2qdyq55XpAhpTYEAJkcPiUY5fjgXfftrKUJTwB_6s9XgTdD6LepwvOfpE0ovJsAf5pUMN-LXteAw3fLq_6_zZRDvU_BApwSV-PW8T_Sdi2tjysTctt-cay34RsCd5GkNRMcpfaS_LeldLibsAFggM1j5dTBrFU92Fdj0deGzA1p7lriEw7_oe3NI44nMhgChwm94GfJXOsf3KPaaLq_Zps26mdAozzvXZzXBWMUn07dfQH-rwiLYrMDyFesEAB3gCF0P60_si_7e9jURymuXeVDxsLUXh7oliFgoVm-) **
It was Memorial Day weekend, 2020. Hundreds of protesters flooded the streets of Austin. What started as a demonstration turned into three days of chaos: buildings looted, police vehicles set on fire, a rioter caught with a Molotov cocktail before he could throw it. It took nearly Austin's entire 2,100-officer police force to keep the city from total collapse.
On May 31st, a mob completely shut down I-35 — a major interstate highway — directly in front of police headquarters. Ambulances couldn't get through. Officers gave verbal orders to disperse. A police helicopter broadcast commands over a loudspeaker. The rioters refused.
**Officer Jeffrey Teng and his partner were ordered in to clear the highway.**
Officer Jeffrey Teng with his wife
When they arrived, the mob started throwing rocks. One of those rocks struck Officer Teng's partner square in the chest. Under attack, outnumbered, doing their jobs — Teng and his fellow officers deployed non-lethal rounds to stop the violence.
That's it. That's the "crime."
Now Jeffrey Teng, along with 4 other Austin police officers, faces felony charges. Meanwhile, District Attorney José Garza has dismissed nearly every charge against the actual rioters. The people who threw rocks, set cars on fire, and shut down a highway walk free. The officers who stopped them are being prosecuted.
This is a political vendetta by a DA who has made it his mission to destroy the men and women who keep order in our streets.
And Jeff Teng is paying the price. His career is on hold. His future is uncertain. His trial has been delayed again and again — meaning this family has been living under this cloud for _years_ with no end in sight.
The National Center for Police Defense is standing with Jeff and his family — funding his legal defense and providing support while this ordeal drags on. But we cannot do it without you.
I'm asking you to [ **donate today** ](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=7ae7a47bc5df4e03993605de9de93006&_e=hDALp-jb2BWyYFmIy8MLPSd2OtCsPmB2Krf5i8yUUaxP2J2neHCXDqgLpeOBJONiP477B7595Y3GJITCIUUFswa5RvwReuyk_gBKaRj0sm5jO_3GuSyR3bFLTqTKIEPQVfV_C4k1f-kRKbujWky1dPgixWV8s7SIt6kkeFPSgya9pZDENla-UQBRQtTb_jVPd2spSUu05xccOSYCWjmbaxV_QDQnOnwgKe9C3VuO-DRa4Nq0GodHLLaRRulkyRJpkYjytQqARzR0UFtWiTuuzCboMS6XN9rrQnAlHmfVxoKgSgeyLuBpmEJnQ1LAftnGvont1BtWYgzMDfaFrhS7sUn6e3_0feTZzPny_dgzui2KxXdNZC1fWEXmRv_E9JV4D01WaaGliFxyJSWbZI0hFvamsJ6P5eHVwhG33yVlCF-aztdRjQ-ge4p1CQmKNCIM). $25. $50. $100. Whatever you can. Your gift goes to Jeff's defense and to supporting his family through this nightmare.

They want to lock him away for using non-lethal bean bag rounds against a violent mob that was blocking an interstate highway, hurling rocks at officers, and bringing Molotov cocktails to the party. I have seen a lot in my years in law enforcement. I have seen politics poison the justice system. But what is being done to Officer Jeffrey Teng of Austin, Texas is one of the most shameless, stomach-turning betrayals of law enforcement I have ever witnessed. - It was Memorial Day weekend, 2020. Hundreds of protesters flooded the streets of Austin. What started as a demonstration turned into three days of chaos: buildings looted, police vehicles set on fire, a rioter caught with a Molotov cocktail before he could throw it. It took nearly Austin's entire 2,100-officer police force to keep the city from total collapse. On May 31st, a mob completely shut down I-35 — a major interstate highway — directly in front of police headquarters. Ambulances couldn't get through. Officers gave verbal orders to disperse. A police helicopter broadcast commands over a loudspeaker. The rioters refused. Officer Jeffrey Teng and his partner were ordered in to clear the highway. Officer Jeffrey Teng with his wife When they arrived, the mob started throwing rocks. One of those rocks struck Officer Teng's partner square in the chest. Under attack, outnumbered, doing their jobs — Teng and his fellow officers deployed non-lethal rounds to stop the violence. That's it. That's the "crime." Now Jeffrey Teng, along with 4 other Austin police officers, faces felony charges. Meanwhile, District Attorney José Garza has dismissed nearly every charge against the actual rioters. The people who threw rocks, set cars on fire, and shut down a highway walk free. The officers who stopped them are being prosecuted. This is a political vendetta by a DA who has made it his mission to destroy the men and women who keep order in our streets. And Jeff Teng is paying the price. His career is on hold. His future is uncertain. His trial has been delayed again and again — meaning this family has been living under this cloud for years with no end in sight. Now let me tell you why this mission means so much to me. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. Several years ago, I learned firsthand about the horrific reality of child trafficking. What I heard broke my heart. Children were being bought and sold.
Families were being torn apart.
Lives were being destroyed. **I couldn't forget it.** **I couldn't stay silent.** I kept asking myself one question: **"What if it were my child?"** That question changed my life. What started as a film project became a mission and a calling. That calling eventually led me to help produce the film _Sound of Freedom_. **Not for fame.**
**Not for awards.**
**But because I believed people needed to see the truth.** For years, many people said the film would never succeed. Doors closed.
Studios walked away.
People told us to give up. **But when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option.** And while the film helped awaken millions of people to this crisis, awareness alone is not enough. That is why we created the **Sound of Freedom Foundation**. Our mission is simple: **To stop the sale of God's children.**

| We love working for Sue. Like, a lot. So we wanted to reach out on her behalf to see: **can you help her raise the funds she needs to get the word out to ALL voters of Rhode Island?** Our boss is awesome, there’s no other way to say it. She works so hard, it makes us want to work even harder to make sure everyone knows about her. But we need help, because time is running out before the primary to reach the voters of Rhode Island. Check out her email below that really explains why we [**really need you to chip in right now.**](https://sue4ri.com/l/cffUJaugFSke)
---

> ****
> | [](https://sue4ri.com/l/Guj255y80lpQ)
> **[Donate to help Sue make it past the primary and on to November →](https://sue4ri.com/l/aL10ezBae5Ye)**
>
> ---
>
> Friend,
>
> When people meet my team and me and hear what we’re all about, they get very excited about this campaign.
>
> We’ve spent months meeting neighbors at house parties and showing up in communities across Rhode Island to talk to as many people as we can about what’s actually possible to accomplish from the Lieutenant Governor’s office.
>
> We’re grinding away, but we have to keep expanding. And right now, we are simply running out of time before the primary to raise the funds we need to bring these conversations to every living room in the state.
>
> **[Can you chip in $10 or more today to help us expand our digital ads and mail program so that we can reach more voters who still need to meet me?](https://sue4ri.com/l/1AkPdNDhvF5Q)**
>
> If you’ve saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:
> [DONATE $10](https://sue4ri.com/l/TekyAv31n8Jz)
> ---
> [DONATE $25](https://sue4ri.com/l/MX5EmaFu74BP)
> ---
> [DONATE $50](https://sue4ri.com/l/v0YEXcZ341uY)
> ---
> [DONATE OTHER](https://sue4ri.com/l/wqm00DF8jKAE)
> ---
>
> Here's the challenge: I can't personally meet every Democratic voter in Rhode Island in the next 85 days before the primary (it’s coming up SO fast).
>
> But with the right resources, we can make sure every voter still has the chance to hear what this campaign is all about, even if it can’t all be in person.
>
> Over the next few weeks, we're going to be allocating our budget to investing in ads and mail so more Rhode Islanders can hear about our vision for what the Lieutenant Governor's office could accomplish with the right person leading it.
>
> |
> **_Every dollar helps us start a conversation with another voter.
>
> Every ad helps us expand our reach.
>
> Every piece of mail helps introduce this campaign to someone who hasn't heard from us yet.
>
> And every minute between now and the primary is one minute closer to running out of time to raise the funds we need. That’s where YOU come in, friend._**
> **[Will you chip in today and help us reach every voter we can?](https://sue4ri.com/l/4Ufg5bheZR18) ** | | [ **DONATE** ](https://sue4ri.com/l/cueGH51TlxtK)
> ---
>
> Thank you for being part of this campaign.
>
> Sue

| | | | | | Friend,
It’s not too late to go vote if you haven’t already. Polls don’t close for another hour. As long as you're in line by 7PM, you will still have the opportunity to vote.
Elections are where you, the people, get to pick who represents you in government. While it may not sound like a glamorous task, voting is one of the most important pillars of our democracy.
Be sure to bring a valid ID to your polling location.
If you need to find your polling place, click [HERE](https://us.list-manage.com/9ZdhxgcZjwT?e=1ade0133c0&c2id=2b362848f83f34181b57cffcc913b28a).
I look forward to seeing the results tonight, and I hope I’ve earned your vote to be your next Republican nominee for U.S. Senate.

God Bless,
Jared HudsonRepublican Candidate for U.S. SenateAlabama First. America First.

Team,

Now that we're headed to November, I want to take a moment to look back on how we got here.

I grew up right here in South Sacramento, the eldest of 16 children born to Hmong refugees who fled the war in Laos. We grew up with modest means in Meadowview and Oak Park. But my parents instilled in me the value of hard work and taught me to always fight for the community that gave our family refuge. That instinct has never left me.

You elected me to the Sacramento City Council, where we created the city's first-ever Children's Fund, led community-run vaccination clinics, and fought for affordable housing. And when the moment came to take that fight to Washington, I got in the ring.

[](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquO38L98SklfBdoDq94y0bmIPp1sMsxRlzUR9IaKq2v2uO12fLhXa9LgPRZYbap6SCa0lgcyaEe3Vs8rdZ-B5OUGhSwmGyi8KhFHcDe2CwVfd21bwuMSlMtchgBdQqb9ssqfNaRDdE6G-PYbXfwlNLyKq2GZtA8E8ZKdbsQvcMGfZEM8PWzXxFU0M10mmQ9pK6-CJlzXCDUb2FAVfg-v6f93ZMeE2ZezupoAKnxsZ1D_xYgEREiX2ItpzTv6DRewgqi0KCH_qX654hVAQqevIoIyrRULTX96k7I2oV-KI30yQ6ydNke-EAbnGcK_rJRO1fo3eLKx3_QtTOsLKU-kxcDXlM46Qab5HhXPjN_5VZjTg/4rj/4qidao_1TDqlufJOHqwVOA/h1/h001._227b0xIiK5de6QGfsJEnr4J1goNWlSi32X-YlDOHPE)
We just placed FIRST in the CA-07 primary against a 21-year incumbent who outspent us 3 to 1. Not because of corporate PACs or political insiders. Because of you.

Working families in Sacramento are ready for something different. Housing and healthcare have become unaffordable for so many of us. These aren't abstract policy debates — they are the lived reality of the people I grew up with, the people I've organized alongside my entire career, and the people I am running to represent in Washington.

**[I'm ready to fight for a better tomorrow because the future cannot wait. clean_body: take a moment to look back on how we got here. | | | | Team, Now that we're headed to November, I want to take a moment to look back on how we got here. I grew up right here in South Sacramento, the eldest of 16 children born to Hmong refugees who fled the war in Laos. We grew up with modest means in Meadowview and Oak Park. But my parents instilled in me the value of hard work and taught me to always fight for the community that gave our family refuge. That instinct has never left me. You elected me to the Sacramento City Council, where we created the city's first-ever Children's Fund, led community-run vaccination clinics, and fought for affordable housing. And when the moment came to take that fight to Washington, I got in the ring. We just placed FIRST in the CA-07 primary against a 21-year incumbent who outspent us 3 to 1. Not because of corporate PACs or political insiders. Because of you. Working families in Sacramento are ready for something different. Housing and healthcare have become unaffordable for so many of us. These aren't abstract policy debates — they are the lived reality of the people I grew up with, the people I've organized alongside my entire career, and the people I am running to represent in Washington. | If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | | | | | Thank you for being a part of this journey. – Mai | Mai is the daughter of Hmong refugees, born and raised in Sacramento. name: Freedom 250
subject: Join Us for Salute to America | July 4th | National Mall, Washington, D.C.
body:
The Ultimate Celebration of the Nation’s 250th
Celebrate the Nation’s 250th with patriotic performances, military flyovers, a historic joint military tribute, and the largest fireworks display in history.
| [](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
---
Freedom 250 Presents
# Salute to America
The Ultimate Celebration of the Nation’s 250th —◆— National Mall | Washington, D.C.
**Saturday, July 4, 2026**
Dear Friend, RSVP now for **Salute to America** , a spectacular Independence Day tribute on the National Mall honoring the Nation’s 250th anniversary. | | [ RSVP Now! ](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
---
| [](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
---
This once-in-a-generation celebration will bring America’s story to life through beautiful storytelling, patriotic performances, military tributes, presidential remarks, and the largest fireworks display in history.
The program will be headlined by President Donald J. Trump and feature appearances by national leaders, decorated veterans, and distinguished guests, each helping tell a different chapter of the American story.
Audiences will travel across 250 years of American history, from the revolutionary ideas of the founders to the courage of America’s servicemembers, the promise of civil rights, the role of faith in shaping national character, and America’s extraordinary scientific and cultural achievements.
The program will honor not only the leaders whose names fill history books, but also the servicemembers, athletes, leaders, entrepreneurs, pastors, teachers, visionaries, and trailblazers whose love of country helped define our Nation’s character and inspired generations. It will celebrate 250 years of American history and chart the course for the next 250.
More than 300 members of America’s premier military bands, orchestras, choruses, and ceremonial units will perform together in what is expected to be the largest joint military music and ceremonial ensemble ever assembled.
The celebration will conclude with the largest fireworks display in history, illuminating the Washington Monument, Lincoln Memorial, and the nation’s capital in a breathtaking grand finale designed exclusively for the Nation’s 250th birthday.
[RSVP Now! RSVP now to reserve your place at this Freedom 250 signature celebration.](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
---
Event Details
---
| When | Saturday, July 4, 2026
---|---
Location | National Mall, Washington, D.C.
Program | Storytelling, patriotic performances, military tributes, presidential remarks, and the largest fireworks display in history
Security | Magnetometers open at 1:00 PM. Government-issued photo ID is required, and a Clear Bag Policy applies.
Arrival | Guests should arrive via Constitution or Independence Avenue and proceed to the 15th Street entry line.
Transit | Public transportation is recommended. To plan your trip using Metro, please visit [ https://www.wmata.com/ ](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
RSVP | Reserve your place with one simple RSVP.
Program Highlights
---
American Veterans Center Salute to America Parade President Donald J. Trump headlining the program U.S. Air Force Thunderbirds and U.S. Navy Blue Angels F-22 Raptor, F-35B Lightning II, and MV-22 Osprey demonstration teams U.S. Stealth Airpower Flyover and U.S. Air Force Tri-Bomber Flyover Full fleet reviews representing the Air Force, Marine Corps, Navy, Army, and Coast Guard More than 300 military musicians and ceremonial performers Largest joint military music and ceremonial ensemble ever assembled Largest fireworks display in history
A Full Day of Patriotic Celebration
---
The day begins with the American Veterans Center Salute to America Parade, a patriotic procession honoring the men and women who have served this nation in uniform. Above the National Mall, guests can experience breathtaking displays of American airpower, including the U.S. Air Force Thunderbirds, U.S. Navy Blue Angels, F-22 Raptor Demo Team, F-35B Lightning II Demo Team, MV-22 Osprey Demo Team, Stealth Airpower Flyover, Tri-Bomber Flyover, and fleet reviews across five branches of the armed forces.
A Historic Joint Military Musical Tribute
---
More than 300 members of America’s premier military bands, orchestras, choruses, and ceremonial units will perform patriotic favorites, military tributes, and American classics together on the National Mall. Set against the Washington Monument and Lincoln Memorial, this historic ensemble will honor generations of servicemembers whose sacrifice helped preserve American freedom for 250 years.
A Fireworks Finale Made for the Nation’s 250th
---
The evening will conclude with the largest fireworks display in history, launched from multiple locations around the National Mall and visible across the nation’s capital. Designed exclusively for the Nation’s 250th birthday, the display will illuminate the Washington Monument, Lincoln Memorial, and iconic monuments that have witnessed generations of American history.

---
See you on the National Mall,
The Freedom 250 Team

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: re: Elon
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
We need a wealth tax NOW

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2930%2E4032634%2ELPpf7F)
---
Just a few days ago, Elon Musk became the world’s first trillionaire. Think about that. We're living at a time when more and more people are just hanging on by their fingernails to survive in this economy. And Elon Musk has more money and more wealth than anyone in human history. I want to be clear: This is not just some fluke. It is a feature of a rigged economy. Donald Trump's "Big, Beautiful Bill" cut healthcare for millions of Americans to give guys like Elon bigger tax breaks. The tax code rewards CEOs for firing workers and replacing them with AI. Loopholes have allowed Jeff Bezos to pay an effective tax rate lower than a Boston public school teacher. And we are left with a country, or a handful of billionaires at the top, popping champagne on their $300 million yacht, while working people take on even more shifts to try to pay off their student loan debt. The top 1% of U.S. earners now have more wealth than the entire middle class. We need to overhaul our tax code. We need a wealth tax, and it's about time that corporations paid their fair share. Elon’s status as the first trillionaire should be a wake-up call that enough is enough. It is time to unrig the economy. And that starts with the ultra-wealthy paying their fair share. **With my two-cent wealth tax on ultra-millionaires, billionaires, and now _trillionaires_ we could make the American Dream a reality.** We could expand child care, lower housing costs, cut child poverty, strengthen Medicare, provide paid family leave, and make college more affordable — all by simply asking the ultra-wealthy to finally pay their fair share. Elon Musk and the rest of the ultra-wealthy have armies of lobbyists and a system rigged to their advantage. What we have is numbers. A grassroots movement — including you — of people who are ready for change _NOW_. [**Add your name today if you agree that no one should be able to accumulate that much wealth while millions of Americans struggle to afford housing, health care, and child care. It's time to unrig the economy.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-wealth-tax26/?source=EW_EMZ31U_ELO_ENG_20260616_F&t=8&akid=2930%2E4032634%2ELPpf7F) | [**ADD YOUR NAME**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-wealth-tax26/?source=EW_EMZ31U_ELO_ENG_20260616_F&t=9&akid=2930%2E4032634%2ELPpf7F)

Thanks for being part of this,
Elizabeth

Hey there Fellow Patriot,

I'm Jackie Mary Auringer, I am twenty-nine years old, and I'm a Hudson Valley native who is running for Congress in New York's 18th District to raise up the place that raised me.

My parents dedicated their lives to serving this community as a teacher and local business owner. **They taught me early on what matters: responsibility, accountability, and pride in where you come from.**

That perspective is what drives my commitment to ensuring the Hudson Valley is represented by someone who knows it, values it, and will always put it first.

For too long, the voices of families in the Hudson Valley have been ignored by politicians who are focused on promoting a political agenda that doesn't reflect what life is really like here, especially as the cost of living continues to rise.

# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2281%2E791427%2EG48Whc)
Friend, let me quickly explain this.
The FEC is the government organization that oversees all campaign finance.
Four times a year, we are **legally required** to file our fundraising numbers. They need to know how much we raised, from how many people, and from who.
The FEC then publishes those numbers online for everyone and anyone to see. That’s a big deal.
Everyone who wants to see me lose my race for reelection — AIPAC, corporate Super PACs, billionaires, MAGA Republicans, the right-wing media, special interests — keeps a close eye on our numbers every time they drop. They are itching to find a weakness in our campaign that they can exploit.
So, our last quarterly FEC filing deadline before primary Election Day is only two weeks away. We have very little time to make sure we’re not sending the wrong message.
That’s why I’m setting an ambitious goal. I want to file our next FEC report with **more individual contributions from grassroots supporters like you than ever before.** And I think we can do it.
[**I’m asking you today: Chip in whatever you can afford to help us start SMASHING this FEC fundraising deadline. Join our movement for peace abroad, affordability at home, and justice for all — every dollar adds up as long as everyone does their part.**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-jun26.ltbpUI&refcode=em260616-1-NOR&t=2&akid=2281%2E791427%2EG48Whc)

name: Sheriff Joe Arpaio
subject: In prison for saving lives?
body:
Not on our watch!
Patriot,
This is a disgrace...and every American who believes in law and order should be furious.
Two police officers—Josh Taylor and Brandon Dingman—are currently serving prison sentences for doing exactly what they were trained and ordered to do: respond to a dangerous call, use non-lethal force, and protecting their community.
Let me tell you what really happened, because the media and the District Attorney certainly won't.
On the night of July 4th, 2019, Officer Josh Taylor responded to a domestic disturbance call in Wilson, Oklahoma. When he arrived, he encountered Jared Lakey: a large, fully grown man walking naked down the street wearing nothing but socks.
Josh immediately recognized this situation for what it was: dangerous and unpredictable. Whether it was drugs, mental illness, or something else—this wasn't a man in his right mind. And Josh knew he couldn't handle it alone. He called for backup.
[Donate to Their Defense](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=cb5e80a58aac49269bbd62834a114ace&_e=O3DyMIzXz053WW0V2FRAAYSq1apYQXpcHOcQYTBZIDT7Vgo7sGsSPENNdrw31J8GEmGuwOilqlt1ARc557YCE4kVMBHGAe1DDFBkLv0Qy0SYU4IoxG-Dt-MYJUkjpEELHOC_elzButqqZqrWaMJ3rdvc6RdGt8Yxd69zw8mQ9rVijOC6m2W1NmMzmuMZQXM_N_ymyOCn1Dlqz7CA5yEnvsgyhMPN-z9imyb4vCBQKhp9z77KnWxyFE-uJm2OmxKoYJRiKypo_-MRsygwHxsGfi6c096Yb9fW93iyWPNywwBPhPZwBH6zGdlW9WEUaUFP4hNUGVxGXpzFA6BFLD5s5yxRj2BAGk28HUnx4nL1EeiyFbdegqHcRs_gebYMEAIIbCh4cTAZFi0izuuND0b6kmXgO50VmH3kXcqipbb9qVyGo1eZUWTJ7lUS0E3AzKm7)
Officer Josh Taylor
Officer Brandon Dingman
Officer Brandon Dingman arrived on scene, and the two officers tried to do what they were trained to do: safely and professionally bring Mr. Lakey into custody.
But Lakey was 350 pounds, combative, and resisting arrest. When verbal commands didn't work and physical restraint proved impossible, they turned to their department-issued, non-lethal tasers.
They deployed them multiple times, but Lakey kept tearing the barbs out. He was clearly not being fully affected by the tasers—and even after repeated attempts, the officers were unable to subdue him.
Eventually, Josh and Brandon were able to get his arms and cuffed him. They immediately called for medical assistance. An ambulance arrived. Lakey was taken to the hospital.
At that point, the officers had done everything they could—and everything right.
But tragically, Jared Lakey passed away two days later. The autopsy was inconclusive. He had an enlarged heart and lung issues. Drug screenings were unreliable due to the fluids pumped into his system at the hospital. There was no determined cause of death.
Even so, the department launched an internal review. Then the City Council reviewed the case too.
Both cleared the officers. That's two separate investigations concluding Josh and Brandon followed procedure.
Case closed, right?
Wrong.
A full year later, a politically motivated District Attorney, smelling an opportunity, dragged the case back up and charged these officers with second-degree murder.
Let that sink in: second-degree murder. He ignored the internal findings. He ignored the medical uncertainty. He ignored the fact that these officers never even laid a hand on Lakey's neck or airway.
They followed their training, used the gear they were issued, and even called for medical help.
But none of that mattered to a DA looking to make headlines.
Now, these two good cops, family men, community protectors, are sitting behind bars.
The National Center for Police Defense is fighting to overturn this injustice. We're supporting their legal appeals, helping their families, and backing efforts to remove the biased District Attorney who never should have touched this case in the first place.
But appeals are costly. And the longer this drags on, the longer Josh and Brandon sit in prison...separated from their families, their children, their lives.
That's why I'm writing you today. We need your help.
[Yes — I'll Donate Today](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=cb5e80a58aac49269bbd62834a114ace&_e=O3DyMIzXz053WW0V2FRAAYSq1apYQXpcHOcQYTBZIDT7Vgo7sGsSPENNdrw31J8GEmGuwOilqlt1ARc557YCE4kVMBHGAe1DDFBkLv0Qy0QurFJrhXZ5HFO-PU2Bx1mVGn726Xvzr8g_D4Sl1hipmpf7SWLzgQW37-KntDalK14cvD9G0VJueXu8EHxzqNCDcqLDLUcS2tkamzdssNGALSNPuhigRB1aWy7Rh7X3qA9p81ySmYYTCsRxvd9KZH7sdVsoHyie6B3ospAwDrFl7LkadupC87NUrRSMUEg81pW6PNzA56sqY9bwkyu5yU_9UZ2OEUxPd-c3ucq3IeqL8RzG5sl02yLqJ8quEhF_v4Uf7tcJSUxfyD_gfTDanYDAGmowtWO2PI8T0mFBucewDDxDZyROY6InNJU0KaZgxAzwQYGGE4SXkyhL_vYNcPpu)
We need to raise funds to fuel the legal defense and appeal process. These officers deserve their freedom. They deserve a fair hearing. And they deserve to come home.
We cannot let this go unanswered. If we don't stand up now, more and more police officers will suffer the same fate: thrown to the wolves by political activists in prosecutor's clothing.
Josh and Brandon were railroaded, plain and simple. And now we need to right this wrong.
Will you step up today and donate to support their appeals?
## Stand With Josh & Brandon
Every dollar goes directly to their legal defense and appeals. Help bring them home.
[Click Here to Donate](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=cb5e80a58aac49269bbd62834a114ace&_e=O3DyMIzXz053WW0V2FRAAYSq1apYQXpcHOcQYTBZIDT7Vgo7sGsSPENNdrw31J8GEmGuwOilqlt1ARc557YCE4kVMBHGAe1DDFBkLv0Qy0Skd-zwB5WuGhK3gtDJ8lNtdTujSKsR-a_VoQwprM7PEVv2X14dm25hqis9pm92dZqFdOc1DrhnUk7lFA6kauZF7C6byow1eq8Ap0xtj4m-DkBB1thvfsKx_38BsmqYDqX9MNkqZbyl5dwz3IkMjkABhlT6XFtyFO4zlTKP2NT8P9C-AwR9jqhfLnQJ5qOJUCc-8u3hMe07TmZbZAZ6UnWX1CwiwrJeJPeOJBdPUcdfTMHDItdfQgo9vWI6HDYjDV-G8Z03h7Zi-ILla1aV5iVxNRG33hV8UVZSaxpQO2Vzc1ZEFoDy37sWhRBDaOJ345gtEBe1-_ItOHvKjJ_eFkzP)
Your generous gift goes to defending these officers and restoring justice. No family should have to go through this. No officer should be imprisoned for doing his job.
Let's send a message: we still back the badge—and we won't let politics destroy the lives of our heroes.
For justice,
Sheriff Joe Arpaio (ret.)
National Center for Police Defense | Defenders for Justice

body:

Team, over the last few months, I've had some time to think.
And the more I thought, the more I kept coming back to something my father used to say at the dinner table when I was growing up in Peoria.
He'd look at us and say: "Think of the greatness of this country. Whatever you do, make sure this country is there for the next families who need it."
He said that as an immigrant who came here with nothing. He said it after our family had struggled, having lived in public housing and on food stamps. He said it because he believed — with everything he had — that this country could still be a place where hard work leads somewhere. Where a kid with a hard-to-pronounce last name still gets a real shot.
I built my entire life around that belief.
And right now, that belief is under direct attack.
Donald Trump and his MAGA allies are gutting the safety net that kept my family afloat.
They're rigging the economy for billionaires while working and middle-class families fall further behind.
They're weaponizing the government against immigrants, against workers, against anyone who dares to believe the American Dream should be available to everyone — not just the powerful and well-connected.
My father's America is being dismantled piece by piece. And I refuse to sit back and watch it happen.
That's why today, I'm launching Equal Opportunity Now — a group dedicated to supporting causes and leaders who will fight like hell to expand opportunity, take on Trump's MAGA agenda, and make sure this country is still there for the next families that need it.
Equal Opportunity Now will support the fights that matter most to working families: making sure every child has food on the table and access to a quality education, lowering prescription drug costs and grocery prices, strengthening good-paying jobs and workers' rights, holding corporate bad actors and corrupt politicians accountable, and fighting bigotry and prejudice in all its forms.
These problems require ambitious, bold solutions, championed by leaders who know that our time is running out.
That's why I need you to become a founding donor of Equal Opportunity Now today.
The leaders and groups who are willing to fight back against Trump's MAGA agenda and deliver real change are out there. But they need funding, infrastructure, and people ready to invest in them early. Founding donors who step up now make it possible. They make it real.
Will you split a contribution of $10, $25, or $50 with Equal Opportunity now and Resist Reclaim Rebuild to start this organization off on the right foot? Your grassroots contribution in this early stage will be CRUCIAL to helping us win. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-eon]
CHIP IN TODAY TO DEFEAT MAGA EXTREMISM! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-eon]
My father was right about this country. It's worth fighting for.
Thanks for joining me in the next chapter of my journey; it means the world to me.
— Raja Krishnamoorthi
